title: Preparation 02: Assess coverage and document sample flow – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: 1. The decisions applied Coverage uses melEDI as the common availability signal. Illuminance retains its own missingness, so an unavailable melEDI value does not erase an observed illuminance value. Table 1 separates the hourly and daily decisions and shows when each affects later use. Table 1: Coverage and plausibility decisions recorded in Preparation 02. Decision Requirement Scientific consequence Daily coverage At least 80% of 1,440 local-clock minutes: 1,152 valid melEDI minutes The participant-day remains available to later metric-specific checks. Hourly coverage At least 50% of 60 local-clock minutes: 30 valid melEDI minutes The hour can support an hourly summary; a failed hour does not erase its observed minutes from daily or minute-based metrics. Coverage signal Finite melEDI values Illuminance retains its own observed and missing values; a missing melEDI value does not remove an observed illuminance value. Sleep-period denominator Diary-defined sleep remains in the complete 24-hour measurement cycle Bedside sleep-environment measurements contribute to coverage. Day-long flat-zero screen Exclude an otherwise passing day only when every finite melEDI value is exactly 0 lx Individual zero readings remain valid; the original day and an inclusive sensitivity flag remain stored. Autumn clock change Repeated local-clock minutes are combined only for the coverage decision Both real observations remain separate in actual time. The daily denominator differs from the preregistered sleep-excluded denominator. Sleep-excluded rules remain prespecified sensitivities; they are not substituted for the primary decision on this page. Preparation 04 later checks whether the timing and amount of remaining support are adequate for each specific metric. This primary full-day denominator choice is documented in DEV-055 .

text: 4. Why measurements were unavailable The stored missing-data records distinguish a missing one-minute record, an observed record whose signal was unusable, an otherwise passing day with only zero melEDI values, and a day below 80% valid melEDI. title: Preparation 03: Learn fixed time-of-day reference profiles – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
section: Purpose and position in the preparation chain
text:
Purpose and position in the preparation chain Preparation 03 learned fixed time-of-day reference profiles from the participant-days retained in Preparation 02 . These profiles describe when melEDI and illuminance were typically observed across the day while giving each participant equal influence. Preparation 04 uses them to judge whether a participant-day was observed at the times that matter for a particular metric. The profiles do not replace an observed measurement and, except for the explicitly permitted additive dose correction, do not change a metric value. The exact scientific inputs were: near-eye Rule A one-minute records ; chest Rule A one-minute records ; the stored Rule A settings . The outputs are the fixed intensity profiles, the strict-threshold timing distribution, metric-specific relevance maps, their support summaries, and the provenance records under artifacts/04_reference_profiles/ . title: Preparation 03: Learn fixed time-of-day reference profiles – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
section: How the reference profiles are defined
text: How the reference profiles are defined The profiles separate time alignment, participant weighting, and support requirements so that each scientific decision is explicit. Table 1 states the rules in the order in which they affected the data. Table 1: Scientific decisions used to learn the fixed reference profiles. Decision Recorded operation Why it is needed Eligible input Use the one-minute near-eye and chest files that passed Preparation 02 Rule A. The complete hybrid 24-hour day includes bedside measurements during diary-defined sleep. The reference must represent the same eligible measurement days that enter metric derivation. Time coordinate Retain every observation in actual time and make a separate local-clock copy for learning 48 fixed 30-minute periods. Actual time preserves chronology; local clock aligns observations that occurred at the same time of day. Participant balance Within each 30-minute period, take each participant's median and then the median across participants. Participants with more recorded days or minutes cannot dominate the population reference. Threshold timing Within every participant-day and period, calculate the fraction of valid melEDI minutes strictly above 250 lx; average days within participant and then participants within profile. A population median may remain below 250 lx even when individual days contain threshold events. Profile variants Store pooled, site-specific, and leave-one-site-out versions for full-day, wake, three hours before sleep, and sleep periods. Preparation 04 can use the pooled profile and examine prespecified site-related sensitivity inputs without relearning profiles. Insufficient support Require 20 participants for pooled and leave-one-site-out full-day profiles and five for site- or diary-period-specific profiles. Retain unsupported periods without interpolation. Missing support remains explicit and cannot be replaced by an invented time-of-day pattern. These are stored production decisions. No profile-learning operation is executed during this render. The complete full day is the intended hybrid 24-hour measurement cycle, including bedside measurements during diary-defined sleep. Wake, sleep, and the three hours before sleep are separate profile domains; they do not redefine which days passed the general coverage rule. title: Preparation 03: Learn fixed time-of-day reference profiles – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
section: Probability of exceeding 250 lx by time of day
text: Probability of exceeding 250 lx by time of day The timing of strict melEDI values above 250 lx cannot be inferred from whether the population median profile itself exceeds 250 lx. Individual participant-days may cross the threshold even when the population median remains lower. Preparation 03 therefore learned a separate probability for each half-hour period: within every participant-day, it calculated the fraction of valid minutes with melEDI strictly greater than 250 lx; it gave days equal weight within each participant; and it then gave participants equal weight within the pooled, site-specific, or leave-one-site-out distribution. Table 6 shows that all 36 stored distributions were estimable and had positive probability in at least some periods. Preparation 04 expands each half-hour probability across its 30 constituent minutes only to measure temporal support. It does not weight or change an observed timing. Table 6: Stored support for strict melEDI >250 lx timing distributions. Profile and placement Supported half-hour periods Periods with non-zero probability per distribution Estimable distributions Pooled across sites — Near-eye 48 of 48 44 1 of 1 Pooled across sites — Chest 48 of 48 46 1 of 1 Each site separately — Near-eye 432 of 432 26–41 9 of 9 Each site separately — Chest 384 of 384 32–41 8 of 8 Leave one site out — Near-eye 432 of 432 42–44 9 of 9 Leave one site out — Chest 384 of 384 43–46 8 of 8 The primary support cutoff is 0.80; the 0.70 and 0.90 sensitivities reuse these same fixed distributions.

title: Preparation 03: Learn fixed time-of-day reference profiles – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
section: How Preparation 04 may use each map
text: How Preparation 04 may use each map The intensity and threshold distributions were converted into metric-specific relevance maps. These maps state which times of day matter for checking the observation support of a metric. They do not all have permission to change a value. Table 7 makes that distinction explicit. Table 7: Stored relevance maps, their use, and whether they may change a metric value. Metric map Use in Preparation 04 Estimable maps May change a metric value melEDI dose May estimate additive dose in unobserved supported periods. 141 of 144 Yes Brightest 10 hours (M10) Checks whether enough relevant times were observed; does not change the value. 141 of 144 No Darkest 10 hours (L10) Checks whether enough relevant times were observed; does not change the value. 141 of 144 No Timing above 250 lx melEDI Checks whether enough relevant times were observed; does not change the value. 36 of 36 No Historical paired-channel map — melEDI Retained historical support record; it is not used by the current MDER method. 141 of 144 No Historical paired-channel map — Illuminance Retained historical support record; it is not used by the current MDER method. 142 of 144 No Only the additive missing-dose correction may alter a metric value. M10, L10, and threshold-timing maps are support-only; the historical paired-channel maps are not used by current MDER. The M10 and L10 maps check whether enough relevant times were observed for the brightest and darkest 10-hour windows. The timing map checks support for the first, last, and mean timing above 250 lx. None of these active support-only maps scales a level, duration, or timing, and no L5 profile or map was produced. For current MDER, the daily value is the arithmetic mean of viable one-minute melEDI-to-illuminance ratios. No reference profile weights, scales, or gates that calculation. The stored paired-channel maps describe an earlier ratio-of-integrals method and are retained only as historical provenance; they are not active Preparation 04 inputs for MDER.

title: Preparation 04: Derive light-exposure metrics – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
section: Purpose and position in the preparation chain
text:
Purpose and position in the preparation chain Preparation 04 converts the eligible one-minute light records from Preparation 02 into the daily, diary-period, 30-minute, hourly, and participant-level metrics used by later analyses. It also records whether each individual metric had enough relevant data to be interpreted. A failed support check makes only that metric unavailable; it does not discard the participant-day from unrelated analyses. For offset geometric means, it also records when floating-point roundoff is normalized to a source-verified exact zero. The exact inputs are the Preparation 02 Rule A coverage files, the Preparation 01 sleep and wear intervals, and the fixed time-of-day profiles and relevance maps learned in Preparation 03. The main outputs are eight R data files containing participant-day, participant, 30-minute, and hourly values for the near-eye and chest placements. Preparation 06 combines those files with site and participant context; this report does not inspect any hypothesis result. flowchart TB P1["Preparation 01
sleep and wear intervals"] --> D["Preparation 04
metric derivation"] P2["Preparation 02
eligible one-minute records"] --> D P2 --> M["Current MDER
viable one-minute ratios"] P3["Preparation 03

need time-profile support"] N --> D M --> D D --> O["Daily, participant,
30-minute, and hourly metrics"] O --> V["Independent MDER

model-ready data"] Important Interpret the full-day metrics as a hybrid measurement During wake and the three hours before sleep, the record represents the logger’s worn placement: near-eye or chest. During diary-defined sleep, it represents the bedside sleep environment. A metric spanning the full day is therefore an environmental-light summary of this planned hybrid record, not a continuous 24-hour measure of ocular exposure.

Only the approved dose correction may change a metric value; these maps do not enter the current MDER calculation. Input paths are read from the current stored settings and inventories; no input is rebuilt during rendering. Preparation 02 had already retained only participant-days with valid melEDI for at least 80% of the fixed 1,440-minute hybrid day. The 50% requirement within an hour governs whether an hourly value can be calculated; it does not remove otherwise valid one-minute measurements from daily or minute-based metrics. All-finite, all-zero melEDI days had also been removed from the primary coverage files while remaining available as a predefined sensitivity. Note Short glossary Metric support: the observed data available at the times relevant to a particular metric; insufficient support makes that metric unavailable but does not remove the participant-day. M10 and L10: the mean melEDI during, respectively, the brightest and darkest 10-hour windows of a participant-day. MDER: the melanopic daylight efficacy ratio, calculated here as the arithmetic mean of viable one-minute melEDI-to-illuminance ratios. Transformed and back-transformed quantities: calculations may be made on a scale chosen for statistical or numerical reasons; back-transformation returns the result to its original practical unit, such as lx.

title: Preparation 04: Derive light-exposure metrics – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Scientific rules applied during production Table 2: Metric construction, temporal support, and missing-data rules applied by the production scripts. Scientific operation Rule and reason Measurement represented The full day is a placement-specific hybrid: near-eye or chest measurement while awake, plus bedside sleep-environment measurement during diary-defined sleep. It is not continuous 24-hour ocular exposure. Actual time and local clock Actual UTC time preserves order, elapsed duration, gaps, adjacency, and both repeated autumn hours. Local clock aligns time-of-day bins, M10/L10, timing, and interdaily stability. Thirty-minute and hourly values A 30-minute arithmetic mean needs 15 of 30 valid minutes. An hourly zero-aware geometric mean needs 30 of 60 and uses a 0.1 lx offset so true zeros remain valid. Unsupported bins stay as missing rows. Numerical zeros after geometric means After adding 0.1 lx, averaging on the log10 scale, and transforming back, production subtracts the offset. A result within the unit-aware floating-point tolerance is stored as exact zero only when every finite source value is exact zero; negative light beyond tolerance stops production. Missing minutes stay missing and never become zero. Thresholds and missing minutes Comparisons are strictly >1,000, >250, <10, and <1 lx melEDI. Missing or invalid minutes are never converted to zero or darkness and never bridge a continuous period. Diary-period metrics Wake, pre-sleep, and sleep values require 80% support in that specific diary period; 70% and 90% are fixed sensitivities. An incomplete diary domain, absent period, or inadequate support affects only that metric. Dose and MDER Observed dose integrates actual durations. Only dose may be corrected for when missing data occurred, with at least 80% profile relevance and a maximum factor of 1.25. MDER is the arithmetic mean of viable one-minute melEDI/illuminance ratios on the 1,440-position local-clock grid. Both channels must be finite and strictly positive, and at least 720 ratios are required. It is not weighted, scaled, profile-gated, or calculated as a ratio of daily integrals. Brightest and darkest 10 hours M10 tests all 841 non-wrapping one-minute starts; L10 tests all 1,440 starts and may cross midnight. Each window is 600 minutes, uses at least 80% ordinary and profile support, and returns a geometric mean and midpoint. The same source-verified numerical-zero rule applies to the geometric mean. No L5 metric is produced. Timing and longest continuous period First, last, and mean timing above 250 lx require sufficient support where such events are expected. The longest observed uninterrupted period is a lower bound; a possible upper bound and exact-only sensitivity preserve uncertainty caused by missing data. Interdaily stability and intradaily variability Both need at least three eligible days. Interdaily stability needs 20 clock hours represented on at least two days; intradaily variability needs 24 truly adjacent hourly pairs across at least three days.

title: Preparation 04: Derive light-exposure metrics – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Source-verified zeros after geometric means Geometric means can include true zero measurements because production first adds 0.1 lx, averages on the log10 scale, transforms back, and subtracts the same 0.1 lx. In exact arithmetic, an all-zero source window returns zero. Floating-point arithmetic can instead leave a minute positive remainder: the eight affected L10 means were 4.163336342344337e-17 lx, far below the source-verified numerical tolerance of 2.220446049250313e-14 lx. The active numerical-zero rule stores a positive remainder within that tolerance as exact zero only when every finite source minute is itself exactly zero. Missing minutes remain missing; they are counted separately and never imputed as zeros. A materially negative result stops production, and a small positive result with any positive source minute is retained. Exactly eight primary L10 mean cells changed: three near-eye and five chest. Seven selected 600-minute windows contained 600 observed zero minutes. The remaining chest window contained 547 observed zero minutes and 53 missing minutes; all 547 observed values were zero, and the 53 missing minutes stayed missing. L10 remains available for all 816 near-eye and 902 chest participant-days, so neither the sample nor its support rule changed. Every non-L10 value and all samples are unchanged. No hypothesis model is run or rebuilt by this report. The sealed audit contains 12 numerical-zero normalizations in total: four previously documented negative roundoff residuals and the eight positive residuals above. A zero-capable analysis retains these participant-days as exact zeros; a later two-part model retains them in its zero/occurrence part and excludes them only from a strictly positive magnitude part by definition. The central distinction is between participant-day eligibility and metric-specific availability. A day that passed the general coverage rule remains in the prepared data even when, for example, its pre-sleep period is unknown, its M10 window has insufficient support, or its paired illuminance data cannot support MDER.

title: Preparation 04: Derive light-exposure metrics – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
section: MDER from viable one-minute channel pairs
text: MDER from viable one-minute channel pairs The melanopic daylight efficacy ratio (MDER) describes melEDI relative to photopic illuminance. For each participant-day, production first represents the complete 1,440-position local wall-clock grid. If the autumn clock change creates two observations for one local minute, melEDI and illuminance are each averaged within that clock minute before their ratio is formed. A local minute that does not exist during the spring clock change remains missing. A minute contributes only when both channels are finite and strictly greater than zero. This restriction defines a viable proportional comparison: a zero illuminance denominator is undefined, and a zero in either channel does not represent a meaningful positive channel ratio for this estimand. MDER is the arithmetic mean of the viable one-minute melEDI/illuminance ratios. At least 720 of the 1,440 positions must be viable; the boundary is inclusive, so exactly 720 passes. If fewer are viable, only MDER is unavailable. The participant-day and all other metrics remain eligible. No time profile weights, gates, or scales enter current MDER, and it is not a ratio of daily channel integrals. Records describing a profile-supported ratio-of-integrals method and 70%, 80%, or 90% MDER gates document an earlier method; they are not active. The gap-timing-unaware dataset still passed the general 50%-per-hour and 80%-per-day coverage rules. Its name means that the timing of remaining missing observations was not used for an additional metric-specific adjustment. For this first explanation only, the primary dataset could be interpreted as a time-sensitive primary metric dataset ; hereafter it is called simply the primary dataset . Both datasets now use the same momentary-ratio MDER definition. Table 6: Current MDER availability and distribution summaries under the same viable one-minute-ratio estimand. title: Preparation 06: Build model-ready datasets – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
section: Purpose and position in the analysis chain
text:
Purpose and position in the analysis chain Preparation 06 turns the checked light-exposure metrics from Preparation 04 and the fixed participant, questionnaire, and diary files acquired in Preparation 05 into inputs that hypothesis analyses can use. It first makes participant files structurally consistent, then adds participant and site context to the metric files, preserves the distinction between local clock time and actual elapsed time, and finally stores a separate input when a hypothesis method has been approved. H01 is the first such build. This step does not fit a statistical model. The predefined gap-timing-unaware dataset still passed the general 50%-per-hour and 80%-per-day coverage rules. Its name means that the timing of remaining missing observations was not used for an additional metric-specific adjustment. For contrast, the primary dataset could be interpreted as a “time-sensitive primary metric dataset.” From this point onward, this report calls it simply the primary dataset . The exact stored inputs are the current light-metric files, the fixed questionnaire and diary files, site and daylight context, elapsed-time records, and the separately prepared gap-timing-unaware dataset. Elapsed time is represented in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC); time-of-day fields retain the site’s local clock time. This structural work is kept separate from later joins so that recorded values, missing values, and excluded free text can be checked before metrics and participant information meet. The procedure did not recalculate questionnaire totals or factor scores. title: Preparation 06: Build model-ready datasets – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
section: 4. Preserve time of day and actual elapsed time
text: 4. Preserve time of day and actual elapsed time Local clock time and elapsed time answer different questions. A 30-minute row labelled 08:00 represents 08:00 at every study site, which is useful for time-of-day comparisons. UTC records how much real time separated two rows, which is necessary for continuity and autocorrelation. A separate temporal-sequence operation preserves both coordinates without changing melEDI values. When clocks move back, a local-clock interval may represent two real intervals; its stored local-clock outcome is their average. When clocks move forward, a local-clock interval can have no corresponding real interval. Only an unambiguous, usable real interval can continue an elapsed-time sequence. A real gap, unusable outcome, repeated autumn interval, or structural spring gap starts or interrupts a sequence. Table 6: Stored links between local-clock outcomes and actual elapsed-time intervals. section: 5. Combine checked data without choosing a hypothesis sample
text: 5. Combine checked data without choosing a hypothesis sample The combination step reads the checked metric files, standardized participant inputs, and site context. It adds one matching participant record and one matching site/date record to each measurement row. It does not apply a complete-case filter or a hypothesis-specific exclusion. Instead, it records which questionnaire and diary inputs are available, allowing each hypothesis to state its own requirements later. The shared primary near-eye input contains 141 participants, 816 participant-days, and 39,168 30-minute grid rows. The complementary chest input contains 154 participants, 902 participant-days, and 43,296 rows. Chest measurements remain complementary; they are not pooled with the primary near-eye measurements. title: Preparation 06: Build model-ready datasets – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
section: Current MDER in the shared inputs
text: Current MDER in the shared inputs The shared inputs use the current metric version. In these files, daily MDER is the arithmetic mean of viable one-minute melEDI/illuminance ratios on a complete 1,440-position local wall-clock grid. Both channels must be finite and strictly greater than zero; a zero-denominator ratio is undefined, and a zero in either channel does not define the positive proportional comparison used by this estimand. When the autumn clock change produces duplicate local minutes, the two channels are averaged separately within that clock minute before the ratio is formed. An absent spring-forward minute remains missing. At least 720 viable ratios are required, and exactly 720 passes the inclusive 50% rule. Failing that rule makes MDER alone unavailable: the participant-day, its other metrics, and its attached participant and site context remain in the shared inputs. Current MDER uses no time-profile weighting, exclusion, or scaling and is not a ratio of daily integrals. The older ratio-of-integrals and profile-based exclusion records document an earlier method and are not active. Table 9: Current MDER availability and distribution summaries in the two stored prepared datasets. Placement Eligible days Days with MDER Days without MDER Participants with MDER Mean MDER Median MDER Primary dataset Near-eye 816 702 114 137 0.7239 0.7239 Chest 902 732 170 152 0.7565 0.7494 Gap-timing-unaware dataset Near-eye 811 687 124 137 0.7243 0.7239 Chest 897 723 174 152 0.7567 0.7495 Primary and gap-timing-unaware rows are read from their stored independent-verification summaries; rendering does not reconstruct MDER. In the primary dataset, MDER is available for 702 of 816 near-eye participant-days from 137 participants (mean 0.7239; median 0.7239) and 732 of 902 chest participant-days from 152 participants (mean 0.7565; median 0.7494). In the gap-timing-unaware dataset, the same momentary-ratio estimand is available for 687 of 811 near-eye participant-days from 137 participants (mean 0.7243; median 0.7239) and 723 of 897 chest participant-days from 152 participants (mean 0.7567; median 0.7495). The stored comparison found all 25,620 non-MDER participant-day cells exactly unchanged and retained all 618 × 47 site/daylight context values exactly. Thus no non-MDER or site-context scientific value changed.

title: Preparation 06: Build model-ready datasets – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
section: Source-verified L10 zeros in the shared inputs
text: Source-verified L10 zeros in the shared inputs L10 is the mean melEDI during the darkest 10-hour window of a participant-day. Its geometric mean can represent true zeros because production adds 0.1 lx, averages log10(melEDI + 0.1) , transforms back, and subtracts 0.1 lx. In exact arithmetic, an all-zero source window therefore returns zero. Floating-point arithmetic left eight primary L10 means at 4.163336342344337e-17 lx instead. This remainder is far below the source-verified tolerance of 2.220446049250313e-14 lx. The active numerical-zero rule stores a positive remainder within that tolerance as exact zero only when every finite source minute is exactly zero. Missing minutes remain missing; they are counted separately and are never imputed as zeros. A small positive remainder is retained if any finite source minute is positive, and a materially negative result stops production. Table 10: Primary L10 values passed into the shared inputs as source-verified exact zeros. Placement New exact-zero L10 cells Stored evidence and effect on the prepared sample Near-eye 3 Three 600-minute windows: 600 observed zeros in each None; all 816 primary participant-days remain Chest 5 Four windows: 600 observed zeros; one window: 547 observed zeros + 53 missing minutes None; all 902 primary participant-days remain Total 8 Seven windows: 600 observed zeros; one window: 547 observed zeros + 53 missing minutes No sample or metric-support contract changed Counts and source-minute evidence are read from the stored independent numerical-zero record; rendering does not recalculate an L10 window. Exactly eight primary L10 mean cells changed: three near-eye and five chest. Seven 600-minute windows contained 600 observed zero minutes. The remaining chest window contained 547 observed zero minutes and 53 missing minutes; all 547 observed values were zero, while the 53 missing minutes stayed missing. All 816 near-eye and 902 chest participant-days remain in the shared inputs. Every non-L10 scientific value, every sample definition, all 30-minute and hourly values, and all gap-timing-unaware scientific values are unchanged. The shared primary inputs inherit the eight exact-zero L10 values without a sample change. No hypothesis model was fitted or refitted. For an analysis that permits zero outcomes, these participant-days remain as zeros. In a two-part analysis, they remain in the zero/occurrence component and are excluded only from the strictly positive magnitude component by that component’s definition.

section: Limitations carried into the model-ready inputs
text: Limitations carried into the model-ready inputs Independent reconstruction of the current reference-profile input remains incomplete. Independent reconstruction of current diary-period support remains incomplete. These qualifications carry forward because the model-ready files use the current reference profiles and diary-period support classifications. They do not indicate that the current data or a downstream result is wrong. Readers can inspect the state, daylight, and placement information in representative one-minute profiles in Preparation 07 .

text: Producing scripts in execution order The producing scripts are listed below in execution order. Their separation is scientific provenance: each step has a narrower responsibility and a stored output that can be checked before the next step begins. Rendering this report reads those outputs only. Derive the current metric layer Script: scripts/ pipeline/ build_metric_derivation.R Module: scripts/ pipeline/ metric_derivation.R; scripts/ pipeline/ time_support.R Reads the eligible one-minute records and reconstructs the current metric layer. For MDER, it uses the complete 1,440-position local-clock grid, averages fall-back duplicates channel-wise, averages viable positive finite one-minute melEDI/illuminance ratios, and requires at least 720 ratios. For offset geometric means, it preserves the raw back-transform and applies the source-verified METRIC-011 numerical-zero rule before storing a non-negative value. This upstream step is shown because its current manifest is an exact input to the shared model data. Stored output: artifacts/ 05_metrics/ and artifacts/ 12_manifests/ metric_artifacts.csv 2. section: Purpose and position in the preparation chain
text:
Purpose and position in the preparation chain This final preparation page is a display-only inspection of the prepared one-minute data. It shows one participant-day from each study site before any hypothesis model is fitted. The profiles combine melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance (melEDI; lx), local daylight, diary-defined periods, and declared non-wear so that readers can see what the accepted minute-level records look like. The exact scientific inputs are the prepared near-eye minute data from Preparation 02, the site- and date-specific daylight context assembled in Preparation 06, and the site metadata used to interpret local time. The fixed selection and its display files are illustrative only: none enters an H01–H11 model. title: Preparation 07: Inspect example days from each study site – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Inputs and selection requirements A participant-day could enter the selection pool only if it passed the general coverage rules from Preparation 02: at least 50% valid observations within each summarized hour and at least 80% valid observations across the full 24-hour day. It also needed all 1,440 local-clock minutes and one complete diary sleep interval with a visible sleep start and wake transition. One day per site was then selected reproducibly; the selection was not repeated to find especially tidy or favourable profiles. The 80% daily rule covers the complete 24-hour measurement cycle. It combines near-eye measurements while participants were awake with bedside measurements during the diary-defined sleep interval. Retaining both contexts preserves the full day; it does not imply that the bedside sleep measurement was made at the eye.

title: Preparation 07: Inspect example days from each study site – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
section: How to read the one-minute profiles
text: How to read the one-minute profiles Civil night is the shaded part of the day when the Sun is more than 6° below the horizon; the unshaded interval is civil day. The strip below zero shows the diary-defined waking daytime, the three hours before sleep, and sleep. Red overwrites the strip where the wear log records “off” outside diary-defined sleep; wear-log entries do not define sleep. The dashed step is a contextual reference rather than a fitted value: 250 lx during waking daytime, 10 lx during the three hours before sleep, and 1 lx during sleep. All panels use the same transformed y-axis so that zero, dim exposure, and high daytime exposure can appear together. The transformation changes only display spacing; the source CSV retains the stored melEDI values in lx.

title: Sensor-placement decision – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Sensor-placement decision Primary near-eye analysis with chest-level measurements as a complementary comparison Last modified: August 13, 2026 Note Answer in brief Near-eye measurements provide the primary estimates of personal ocular light exposure. Chest measurements provide complementary evidence. The two sensor positions remain separate because they do not measure an interchangeable exposure, and combining them into one larger sample would not be scientifically justified.

title: Sensor-placement decision – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
section: Why the sensor positions stay separate
text: Why the sensor positions stay separate A sensor near the eyes more directly represents the light available to the eyes than a sensor worn on the chest. Body orientation, clothing, and local shading can affect the chest measurement differently. The size and direction of a position difference can also depend on the exposure measure, setting, participant, and day. Near-eye and chest measurements therefore are not treated as interchangeable, and similar estimates are not interpreted as evidence that the positions are equivalent. The Descriptive results provide study-level context for the measurements recorded at the two positions.

title: Sensor-placement decision – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: How the positions are compared Placement-specific models are fitted separately: near-eye models provide the primary result, while chest models provide the complementary result. A direct near-eye–chest comparison uses a common sample containing the same participants and participant-days at both positions. A participant-day means one participant’s record for one calendar day. Repeated observations from the same participant and participant-day remain related in the analysis rather than being treated as independent. Results are reported in practical units with 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs). The relevant hypothesis report gives the exact numbers of participants, participant-days, observations, sites, and complete near-eye–chest pairs for the analysis it presents. Preparation 02: coverage and sample flow explains how measurement coverage and availability determine those samples.

title: Sensor-placement decision – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: What sleep-period measurements represent During sleep, the devices are not worn at their nominal near-eye and chest positions. Values recorded during the sleep period therefore describe the bedside sleep environment. They are not interpreted as light measured on the body at the usual waking sensor positions.

text: Table 2: metric distributions Table 4 presents the registered metric categories and order, ten site columns, scaling column, and miniature distribution column. Every numerical cell states N , the number of participants, and d , the number of participant-days with a finite value. The site columns have equal widths and each median, interval, mean ± SD, and size line is kept intact. A compact line under each metric name states what the metric captures and why that construct is physiologically or health-relevant; these notes are context, not health- effect estimates from this descriptive dataset. MDER is the arithmetic mean of viable one-minute melEDI / photopic illuminance ratios, with both channels finite and strictly positive. Each day is evaluated on a complete 1,440-minute local wall-clock grid and retained with at least 720 viable ratios (the inclusive 50% rule). Fall-back duplicate local minutes are averaged within channel before the ratio is formed; spring-forward absent minutes remain missing. For the L10 mean, source windows verified as entirely zero are retained as exact 0 lx. Machine-precision residuals from the averaging calculation are not interpreted as positive exposure. title: Preregistration deviations and current analysis decisions – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: How to read this page A preregistration records the analysis plan before the results are known. A deviation is a scientifically relevant difference between that plan and the analysis now used. This page states those differences directly and keeps their stable IDs so that result and preparation reports can link to the exact decision that affects them. The first section contains current scientific deviations. The second keeps one qualification that is still open. The third records consequential implementation issues that have been resolved or superseded and therefore do not describe the current method. The final section contains environment, source, and documentation provenance. Note Current interpretation Use Current analysis and What this means for interpretation to understand the accepted analysis. The Preregistered or expected field is preserved to show what differed; resolved-history entries must not be read as the current method.

title: Preregistration deviations and current analysis decisions – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Statistical terms used across entries Tip Short glossary A site-average estimate is an average across sites that gives each site equal weight. A predictor-by-site interaction allows the association with a predictor to differ among study sites. A false-discovery-rate (FDR) adjustment accounts for a declared family of statistical tests; later entries use FDR . Model checks (model diagnostics) assess whether the fitted model is adequate for its intended interpretation. Participant-cluster-robust uncertainty allows repeated observations from the same participant to remain associated without treating them as independent. A sensitivity analysis repeats an analysis after one stated choice is changed to assess whether the interpretation is stable. Tip Time curves and transformed results A nonlinear generalized additive model (GAM) analysis lets the estimated exposure pattern vary flexibly over time rather than forcing a straight line; later entries may use GAM . AR(1) is a model for autocorrelation in which observations closer together in a sequence are expected to be more similar; the similarity decreases with separation. A derivative is the estimated rate at which a fitted curve is changing at a given point. A Shapley allocation distributes fitted-model variation among model components by averaging their added contribution across possible entry orders. A back-transformed quantity has been converted from the model’s transformed scale to an interpretable response-scale quantity, such as a ratio or time difference. A 95% confidence interval (95% CI) gives the range of parameter values compatible with the estimate under the stated model and uncertainty procedure.

title: Preregistration deviations and current analysis decisions – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Light-exposure measures named in entries Tip Measure glossary Melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance (melEDI) describes light in terms of its stimulation of the melanopsin pathway and is reported in lux. M10 and L10 describe the brightest and darkest supported consecutive 10-hour windows, respectively. Melanopic daylight efficacy ratio (MDER) is the mean of viable one-minute ratios of melEDI to photopic illuminance in the current analysis. Interdaily stability (IS) describes regularity across days; intradaily variability (IV) describes fragmentation across adjacent hours within days. MCTQ and MEQ are distinct chronotype measures: corrected midsleep timing from the Munich Chronotype Questionnaire and morningness preference from the Morningness–Eveningness Questionnaire. LEBA is the Light Exposure Behaviour Assessment, and VLSQ-8 is an eight-item self-report measure of visual light sensitivity.

text: DEV-001: All hypotheses; placement Topic. All hypotheses; placement Current disposition. Implemented Preregistered or expected. Chest data primary; repeat with glasses for robustness Current analysis. Near-eye glasses measurements are primary for the ocular-exposure estimand. Chest measurements are complementary and are compared on placement-matched samples when a direct placement comparison is shown. Why. The placements measure related but non-interchangeable light fields, so simple pooling or unmatched identity comparisons are not valid. Affected hypotheses. All hypotheses (H01–H11) What this means for interpretation. Primary conclusions come from near-eye data; chest evidence is labelled complementary and does not replace the primary estimand. section: DEV-004: Site sample size and placement availability
text: DEV-004: Site sample size and placement availability Topic. Site sample size and placement availability Current disposition. Implemented Preregistered or expected. Target 15-30 participants per site using all eligible repository participants Current analysis. Recruitment and placement availability remain uneven by site. Every accepted hypothesis analysis now reports its exact participants, participant-days or participant-hours, observations, placements, and sites rather than presenting one universal sample size. Why. Uneven support is an observed feature of the study design and cannot be repaired analytically; exact model-specific denominators and complementary-placement labels are the approved response. Affected hypotheses. All hypotheses (H01–H11) What this means for interpretation. Site and placement comparisons must be interpreted with their model-specific support, especially for Munich (DE), San José (CR), and glasses-versus-chest comparisons. Related records. None Current evidence sources audit/decisions/site_display_conventions.md audit/handoffs/H01_worker_handoff.md audit/handoffs/H02_worker_handoff.md

title: Preregistration deviations and current analysis decisions – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
section: IMP-012: Metric construct; full-day and sleep
text: IMP-012: Metric construct; full-day and sleep Topic. Metric construct; full-day and sleep Current disposition. Implemented Preregistered or expected. The intended 24-hour environmental-light record combines worn near-eye waking measurements with bedside sleep-environment measurements during the diary-defined sleep window Current analysis. The full-day hybrid record combines worn waking measurements with retained bedside sleep-environment measurements and is described explicitly as such. Why. This preserves the practical 24-hour environmental record without mislabelling sleep values as ocular exposure. Affected hypotheses. All hypotheses (H01–H11) What this means for interpretation. Full-day metrics are hybrid personal/environmental summaries; sleep-specific interpretations remain environmental. Related records. DEV-005 and REP-003 Current evidence sources audit/decisions/placement_decision.md audit/decisions/daily_coverage_denominator.md

title: Preregistration deviations and current analysis decisions – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: REP-001: Placement pooling Topic. Placement pooling Current disposition. Implemented Preregistered or expected. No pooled placement model was preregistered; chest was primary and glasses a robustness repeat Current analysis. Simple pooling of near-eye and chest measurements is rejected; placements retain separate estimands. Why. The placements differ systematically and are not duplicate measures of one interchangeable quantity. Affected hypotheses. All hypotheses (H01–H11) What this means for interpretation. No pooled placement claim is permitted. Related records. DEV-001 Current evidence sources audit/decisions/placement_decision.md

title: Preregistration deviations and current analysis decisions – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: REP-002: Chest complementary analysis Topic. Chest complementary analysis Current disposition. Implemented Preregistered or expected. Registered glasses analysis was a robustness repeat Current analysis. Direct near-eye/chest displays use placement-matched participant, local-date, and clock keys, while chest remains complementary in all-available analyses. Why. Matching makes the compared placements refer to the same observed periods and avoids conflating placement with sample composition. Affected hypotheses. All hypotheses (H01–H11) What this means for interpretation. Matched comparisons describe placement sensitivity, not equivalence, and unmatched all-available estimates are not plotted against each other as identities. Related records. DEV-001 Current evidence sources audit/decisions/paired_placement_comparison_display.md

title: Preregistration deviations and current analysis decisions – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: REP-003: Sleep-period construct language Topic. Sleep-period construct language Current disposition. Implemented Preregistered or expected. Registered outcomes referred to chest-mounted measurements, including sleep metrics Current analysis. Retained sleep-period logger values are described as bedside sleep-environment exposure. Why. This language matches what the logger can measure when wear is not verified during sleep. Affected hypotheses. All hypotheses (H01–H11) What this means for interpretation. Sleep-period results must not be called ocular exposure. Related records. DEV-005 and IMP-012 Current evidence sources audit/decisions/placement_decision.md

title: Preregistration deviations and current analysis decisions – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: DEV-005: Preprocessing; non-wear Topic. Preprocessing; non-wear Current disposition. Implemented Preregistered or expected. Remove non-wear periods identified by device logs Current analysis. Logged non-wear outside reported sleep is set to missing, whereas logger values during the reported sleep interval are retained as measurements of the sleep environment and are not described as worn ocular exposure. Why. The retained sleep values answer a different construct question from waking personal exposure; the placement decision and reader reports now distinguish those constructs. Affected hypotheses. All hypotheses (H01–H11) What this means for interpretation. Sleep-environment results describe light at the logger location during attempted sleep, not verified eye-level exposure while the device was worn. Related records. None Current evidence sources audit/decisions/placement_decision.md audit/decisions/metric_validity.md

title: Preregistration deviations and current analysis decisions – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: DEV-006: Preprocessing; sleep windows Topic. Preprocessing; sleep windows Current disposition. Implemented Preregistered or expected. Registered rule refers to sleep but does not define attempted-sleep versus estimated-onset boundary Current analysis. Attempted-sleep time is the operational boundary for sleep-environment and pre-sleep metrics rather than estimated physiological sleep onset. Why. Attempted sleep aligns the analysed interval with the intention to sleep and is now defined consistently in preparation and reader-facing methods. Affected hypotheses. All hypotheses (H01–H11) What this means for interpretation. Sleep and pre-sleep denominators refer to attempted sleep; they should not be interpreted as intervals anchored to measured sleep onset. Related records. None Current evidence sources audit/decisions/metric_implementation_parameters.md Preparation 04: Metric derivation

title: Preregistration deviations and current analysis decisions – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: IMP-002: Preprocessing saturation boundary Topic. Preprocessing saturation boundary Current disposition. Implemented Preregistered or expected. Set melanopic EDI values above 120000 lx to missing Current analysis. ActLumus melEDI values at or above 100000 lx are treated as outside the instrument’s valid operating range and set to invalid rather than retained. Why. The strict upper-bound rule follows the approved saturation decision and is applied before metric calculation. Affected hypotheses. All hypotheses (H01–H11) What this means for interpretation. Extremely high invalid readings do not contribute to exposure metrics or model samples. Related records. None Current evidence sources audit/decisions/saturation_boundary.md

title: Preregistration deviations and current analysis decisions – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: IMP-017: Timestamp integrity; DST fall-back Topic. Timestamp integrity; DST fall-back Current disposition. Implemented Preregistered or expected. International site-local timestamps retain their absolute instants and remain uniquely keyed through daylight-saving transitions Current analysis. Timestamp processing uses UTC to preserve real instants and a separate local wall-clock axis for cross-site clock-time summaries. Repeated fall-back minutes are averaged only for clock-aligned profiles and retained as separate real intervals for elapsed-time and sequential metrics. Why. The dual-axis rule prevents daylight-saving transitions from either duplicating wall-clock profiles or erasing real elapsed intervals. Affected hypotheses. All hypotheses (H01–H11) What this means for interpretation. Clock-aligned and elapsed-time metrics can legitimately treat the repeated hour differently; the distinction is recorded in preparation provenance. Related records. None Current evidence sources audit/findings/timestamp_dst_fallback.md audit/decisions/metric_implementation_parameters.md

title: Preregistration deviations and current analysis decisions – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: IMP-018: State precedence; measurement context Topic. State precedence; measurement context Current disposition. Implemented Preregistered or expected. The sleep diary defines the relevant sleepprep-to-wake bedside window; wear logs are not sufficiently consistent to define sleep Current analysis. Diary state is authoritative for sleep context. Wear=‘sleep’ is provenance only; wear=‘off’ invalidates waking measurements outside diary sleep, while off or missing wear during diary sleep and site-leave records are retained according to the approved context rules. Why. The rule separates measurement-context validity from the participant’s diary-defined state. Affected hypotheses. All hypotheses (H01–H11) What this means for interpretation. Waking non-wear is excluded, whereas retained sleep values remain environmental rather than verified worn exposure. Related records. DEV-005 Current evidence sources audit/findings/state_precedence_and_channel_mask.md audit/decisions/placement_decision.md

title: Preregistration deviations and current analysis decisions – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
section: DEV-019: H02 and H11 participant-day inclusion
text: DEV-019: H02 and H11 participant-day inclusion Topic. H02 and H11 participant-day inclusion Current disposition. Implemented Preregistered or expected. The registration excludes days using declared coverage rules and does not exclude a day merely because its binned outcome is constant Current analysis. H02 and H11 preserve supported constant profiles and exclude only otherwise eligible participant-days whose finite one-minute melEDI values are all exactly zero under the approved upstream plausibility rule. Why. Individual zero observations are valid; the day-level exclusion targets only an implausible complete zero signal and is retained as a data sensitivity. Affected hypotheses. H02 and H11 What this means for interpretation. The accepted samples do not apply a general constant-profile deletion. Related records. DEV-057 Current evidence sources audit/decisions/all_zero_medi_day_exclusion.md audit/handoffs/H02_worker_handoff.md audit/handoffs/H11_worker_handoff.md

title: Preregistration deviations and current analysis decisions – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: DEV-055: Daily 80% coverage denominator Topic. Daily 80% coverage denominator Current disposition. Implemented Preregistered or expected. The signed preregistration excludes participant-days below 80% valid wear time with sleep excluded from the daily denominator Current analysis. Primary daily coverage uses finite melEDI in eligible hours against a fixed 1440-wall-minute day for the hybrid waking-plus-bedside-sleep record. Sleep-excluded denominators are fixed sensitivities. Why. The author retained the hybrid 24-hour construct as primary while requiring alternative denominators to show dependence on sleep handling. Affected hypotheses. All hypotheses (H01–H11) What this means for interpretation. Primary daily metrics intentionally treat unobserved eligible minutes as missing against the full wall-clock day and should be interpreted as hybrid full-day exposure summaries. Related records. IMP-012 Current evidence sources audit/decisions/daily_coverage_denominator.md

title: Preregistration deviations and current analysis decisions – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: DEV-056: TUM exercise-diary participant key Topic. TUM exercise-diary participant key Current disposition. Implemented Preregistered or expected. Questionnaire and diary source records should be joined under their correct immutable site-participant identifiers Current analysis. The corrected upstream TUM exercise diary assigns the seven affected May 2024 records to TUM_S001, not TUM_S101; no local identifier rewrite is applied. Why. The current melidosData source contains the corrected participant key and is pinned directly. Affected hypotheses. H06 What this means for interpretation. H06 exercise analyses use the authoritative corrected participant identity without altering shared data locally. Related records. None Current evidence sources audit/handoffs/H06_worker_handoff.md audit/reconciliation/preparation06/tum_exercise_source_transition_columns.csv

title: Preregistration deviations and current analysis decisions – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: DEV-057: Participant-day light-signal plausibility Topic. Participant-day light-signal plausibility Current disposition. Implemented Preregistered or expected. The preregistration and submitted implementation use coverage and signal-validity rules but do not specify exclusion of an otherwise eligible complete day-long exact-zero melEDI series Current analysis. The main analysis excludes an otherwise eligible participant-day only when every finite one-minute melEDI value is exactly 0 lx. Individual zeros remain valid, raw rows remain auditable, and the former inclusion is a fixed data sensitivity. Why. A complete exact-zero day is treated as a signal-plausibility failure rather than ordinary darkness. Affected hypotheses. All hypotheses (H01–H11) What this means for interpretation. Affected samples lose only the documented all-zero participant-days; zero-capable metrics and models otherwise retain zero observations. Related records. None Current evidence sources audit/decisions/all_zero_medi_day_exclusion.md
