section: 3. Response transformation and nonlinear model construction
text: 3. Response transformation and nonlinear model construction

title: H02 analysis preparation and provenance – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Exact selected formula H02 used a nonlinear GAM analysis . A generalized additive model (GAM) allows the association with local clock time to bend across the day rather than forcing it to follow a straight line. The fitted response is log10(melEDI + 0.1 lx) ; a back-transformed curve applies the inverse transformation and returns to melEDI in lux. scripts/hypotheses/H02/h02_modeling.R contains the fitting functions; h02_contract.R supplies their fixed specification. The exact Wilkinson formula was: response ~ s (time_hour, bs = "cc" , k = 12 ) + s (time_hour, site, bs = "sz" , k = 12 ) + s (time_hour, participant, bs = "fs" , k = 10 ) + s (participant_day, bs = "re" ) The first smooth is the global time effect , the site-average daily curve: it gives every site equal weight and joins smoothly at midnight. The sz term estimates site-specific departures that sum to zero, so no site is treated as the reference. The participant factor smooth represents remaining differences in daily shape among people after the time and site patterns are considered. The participant-day random effect represents remaining day-to-day level shifts within a participant after those patterns are considered; it moves an entire fitted day up or down. Only the global time effect is forced to join at midnight in the primary model. A sensitivity analysis also makes the site and participant deviations cyclic.

text: 4. Ordering and residual dependence

title: H02 analysis preparation and provenance – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
section: Why local time and true time are both needed
text: Why local time and true time are both needed Autocorrelation means that adjacent 30-minute residuals can remain more alike than residuals farther apart. The AR(1) structure represents this correlation as strongest for adjacent observations and weaker at longer lags. It must restart wherever two observations are not part of the same continuous recorded sequence. Local wall-clock time answers the scientific question about time of day. It cannot by itself establish elapsed ordering across daylight-saving folds, gaps, or missing bins. h02_data.R therefore carries the verified true-UTC source-bin links into each model frame, orders observations by true elapsed time, and defines a new residual sequence: at the start of every participant-day; after a missing or otherwise discontinuous 30-minute interval; and on both sides of a wall-clock outcome that has no one-to-one elapsed-time coordinate. The table is read from the recorded boundary check. “Continuous” rows are ordinary observations inside an existing sequence and are included only to make the denominator visible. section: 5. From fitted models to reported quantities
text: 5. From fitted models to reported quantities

title: H02 analysis preparation and provenance – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Site curves and pointwise intervals h02_modeling.R and h02_figure4_pointwise.R evaluate the stored model on a common 48-bin clock grid. The global time effect is the site-average curve , an average across sites that gives every site equal weight. A site curve is that global effect plus the site’s sum-to-zero departure. Participant and participant-day terms are set to their reference contributions when constructing site curves. A pointwise 95% confidence interval (95% CI) describes uncertainty at one displayed clock time. It comes from the fitted linear-predictor matrix and coefficient covariance with smoothing parameters held fixed; it is not a simultaneous band for the full day and does not multiplicity-control every red segment. The plotted curves are back-transformed to melEDI in lux for reader interpretation. build_h02_figure4_replication.R applies the same builder to near-eye and chest models. It reads stored fits and contributions; it does not refit the model. Its principal outputs are: artifacts/10_figures/H02/figure4_exact_layout_replication.png ; artifacts/10_figures/H02/figure4_exact_layout_replication_chest.png ; matching PDF files; and artifacts/11_source_data/H02/figure4_exact_layout_source*.rds .

title: H02 analysis preparation and provenance – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Fitted-curve variation For every scenario, run_h02_analysis.R extracts the fitted global, site, participant, and participant-day contributions. It then calculates precisely defined curve-dispersion summaries on the modelling scale. Within-site participant and day summaries use site-average weighting, so every site contributes equally. The stored 95% intervals resample sites, participants within sites, and participant-days within participants 2,000 times. The fitted contributions remain fixed. Thus, the bootstrap describes cluster-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fitted smooth structure; it is not a model-refitting bootstrap. The stored resampling draws are under artifacts/08_diagnostics/H02/*__variation_bootstrap.rds .

title: H02 analysis preparation and provenance – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Shapley allocation of fitted-model relevance run_h02_dominance_analysis.R is intentionally narrower: it runs only for the main all-available near-eye and complementary chest samples. The global time effect is mandatory in all subset models. The script fits every one of the eight possible combinations of site pattern, participant pattern, and participant-day shift, then allocates their increments in row-weighted in-sample R^2 across all orders of entry. This Shapley allocation is the average contribution of a component across all orders in which the components could be added, so shared fitted-model information is allocated rather than counted repeatedly. The implementation is also recorded technically as exact general dominance. The 2,000-draw hierarchical bootstrap resamples clusters while holding the eight sets of fitted predictions fixed. The calculation is descriptive in-sample relevance, not causal importance and not cross-validated predictive importance. Stored results and execution evidence are under: artifacts/09_tables/H02/dominance_*.csv ; artifacts/11_source_data/H02/*__dominance_predictions.rds ; artifacts/08_diagnostics/H02/*__dominance_bootstrap.rds ; and artifacts/12_manifests/H02/H02_dominance_manifest.csv .

title: H02 analysis preparation and provenance – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: 6. Model checks and influence assessment run_h02_temporal_diagnostics.R reads the stored selected models and model frames. It verifies coefficient rank and convergence, basis dimensions, sum-to-zero constraints, midnight continuity, boundary-aware residual behaviour, concurvity, and participant/site influence. Concurvity is overlap among nonlinear model terms that makes their separate contributions harder to distinguish. gratia is used for the formal concurvity wrapper; mgcv supplies the fitted GAM machinery and core model checks (diagnostics). build_h02_reader_diagnostics.R converts the diagnostic source objects into the compact near-eye and chest model-check figures used in the H02 results report. Neither script changes the selected formula. The near-eye position is not a retinal measurement, the chest position is not ocular exposure, exact zeros produce a prominent lower-bound response mass, some within-day residual correlation remains, and overlap between global and site nonlinear terms limits interpretation of isolated coefficients. Shapley allocations describe in-sample fitted-model relevance, not causal or cross-validated importance.

title: H02 analysis preparation and provenance – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
section: How to examine or reproduce H02
text: How to examine or reproduce H02 A reader can examine the analysis in four passes: inspect h02_contract.R and input_hashes.csv to confirm the frozen input files and model specification; compare the descriptive samples and support displays above with sample_counts.csv and the model-frame RDS files; follow the producing script named in each output manifest, checking that its recorded inputs and outputs match the quantity being estimated; and read the H02 results report alongside the result tables, model-check outputs, and source-data objects rather than attempting to infer results from a figure image alone. Changes to source data or processing rules should be made before the hypothesis-specific model frames are built and then propagated to every affected analysis. Changing H02 alone would otherwise break comparability with the other hypotheses. Alternative H02 model choices should remain clearly labelled sensitivity analyses until their estimands and model checks are established. Tip Reader takeaway The H02 result was not generated inside a single opaque notebook. It came from a verified set of source files, H02-only model frames, a reusable temporal-model implementation, separately recorded inference and model checks, stored cluster-bootstrap evidence, and checksummed outputs. This page shows how those pieces connect without changing the reported scientific result.

text: H03: Self-reported light source and measured personal light exposure Associations with one-hour melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance Last modified: August 14, 2026

title: H03: Self-reported light source and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Question The preregistered hypothesis was: H3: Hourly self-reported light exposure categories predict hourly geometric mean melanopic EDI. For each accepted participant-hour, participants reported one primary light source. This analysis asks whether the seven registered categories are associated with measured one-hour melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance (melEDI) after accounting for study site. Note Answer in brief The seven light-source categories were associated with near-eye melEDI, F (6, 139) = 97.54, p <0.001 . The association between light-source category and melEDI was allowed to differ by study site in a category-by-site interaction model. Because that interaction was supported, descriptive category and site summaries come from this model; only the preregistered primary omnibus comes from the additive population-mean model. Outdoor daylight had the highest site-average near-eye melEDI, while sleep darkness had the lowest. Supported site-specific deviations showed that the magnitude of the category association varied materially across study sites. Complementary chest summaries had the same broad ordering for the six categories for which a site-average estimate could be calculated across all eight chest sites. A site-average estimate for external light during sleep could not be calculated because one chest site-category cell was absent. The gap-timing-unaware dataset did not change the primary omnibus conclusion or any primary category classification.

title: H03: Self-reported light source and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: What was analysed The primary near-eye sensor position measures light close to the eyes. The complementary chest sensor position measures light at the chest and is not a measure of ocular exposure. Chest measurements are analysed separately; the positions are not pooled and similarity is not interpreted as equivalence. Sleep-category measurements describe the bedside sleep environment rather than light measured at a worn near-eye or chest position. The response is the accepted zero-aware geometric mean melEDI within each hour, including genuine zero values. A participant-hour is one accepted participant-by-local-hour record; a participant-day comprises one participant’s accepted hours on one local date. The primary model contains 17,935 near-eye participant-hours from 140 participants, 801 participant-days, and nine sites. The complementary model contains 19,512 chest participant-hours from 151 participants, 880 participant-days, and eight sites. The outcome derivation and model-ready inputs are documented in Preparation 04 and Preparation 06 . A predefined sensitivity uses the gap-timing-unaware dataset . This dataset still passed the general 50%-per-hour and 80%-per-day coverage rules. The term means that the timing of the remaining missing observations is not used for an additional metric-specific adjustment; it does not mean that gaps, missingness, or coverage were ignored. For this contrast only, the approved preparation could be interpreted as a time-sensitive primary metric dataset. Below, it is called simply the primary dataset. All seven categories meet the pooled support rule. Outdoor electric light is the sparsest category, with 203 near-eye and 219 chest hours. Sparse category-by-site cells remain in the pooled models but are labelled non-estimable for site-specific contrasts when they contain fewer than 20 participant-hours, five participants, or five participants shared with the site’s indoor-electric reference.

title: H03: Self-reported light source and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
section: Primary population-mean and category-by-site interaction models
text: Primary population-mean and category-by-site interaction models The primary analysis is a population-mean quasi-Tweedie GLM with a log link, fixed site effects, fixed light-source effects, and variance power 1.539919. Indoor electric light is the category reference. The primary omnibus asks whether the six non-reference light-source coefficients are jointly zero. Participant-clustered HC1 covariance and finite-cluster t and F reference distributions account for the fact that observations from the same participant may be related. This changes uncertainty; it does not remove temporal patterns from residuals. A separate category-by-site interaction model allows the association between light-source category and melEDI to differ by study site. Near eye uses the full site * light_source interaction, while chest uses an equivalent observed-cell parameterization because one site-category cell is absent. This model supplies the descriptive category and site summaries; the additive population-mean model supplies the preregistered primary omnibus. Cross-site results are reported as site-average estimates . Each included site contributes equally on the fitted log-mean scale, followed by one back-transformation that returns the estimate to melEDI in lux. The resulting absolute estimate is the geometric mean of the fitted site-specific expected values and is not weighted by the number of observations at each site.

title: H03: Self-reported light source and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Principal results The additive primary model and the category-by-site interaction model do not impose the same mean structure. The additive model forces every site to share one category ratio and estimates that common ratio from all participant-hours; its site-average indoor-electric estimate is 88.9 lx. The interaction model first estimates each site-category cell and then gives every site equal weight on the fitted log-mean scale; its corresponding estimate is 85.1 lx. The difference reflects the supported category-by-site interaction, not a different sample or outcome. The preregistered additive-model omnibus remains the primary inferential test. Because that common-effect model is descriptively restrictive, all category means, ratios, 95% CIs, and site summaries from this point use the accepted category-by-site interaction model. The principal display is Figure 1 , followed by the detailed values in Table 1 . Figure 1: Site-average one-hour melEDI and ratios to indoor electric light from the category-by-site interaction model; bars are participant-cluster-robust 95% CIs. These separate placement fits do not establish that the two sensor positions are interchangeable. Result source data and figure source data retain the unrounded estimates and untransformed melEDI values.

title: H03: Self-reported light source and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Exploratory participant random-intercept assessment An auxiliary near-eye model quantified stable participant-level differences: geo_medi_1h ~ site * light_source + (1 | participant) . It used the accepted 17,935 participant-hours from 140 participants, a Tweedie distribution with a log link, and the primary working power fixed at 1.539919. The model contains neither a participant-day intercept nor a temporal correlation term. It was fitted only for variance description and does not replace the accepted population-mean analysis or estimate participant-specific light-source slopes. The model construction and stored-output provenance are documented in the exploratory participant random-intercept assessment . Table 5: Exploratory participant random-intercept variance assessment for the near-eye outcome. Quantity Estimate Interpretation Model-based R² Marginal R² 0.796 Site, light source, and their interaction Conditional R² 0.876 Fixed effects plus the participant intercept Participant increment 0.080 Conditional minus marginal R² Marginal R² Shapley allocation Study site 0.056 7.1% of full marginal R² Light source 0.710 89.3% of full marginal R² Study site × light source 0.029 3.7% of full marginal R² Participant-level variation Adjusted participant ICC 0.394 Participant share after excluding fixed-effect variance Unadjusted participant ICC 0.080 Participant share of total model-based variance Participant SD on log scale 0.694 Spread of stable participant intercepts One-SD multiplicative factor 2.00× Expected-mean factor for a participant one SD above average Participant/fixed variance ratio 0.101 Participant-intercept variance divided by fixed-predictor variance Point estimates use Nakagawa’s model-based variance decomposition with a lognormal distribution-specific variance approximation; no bootstrap intervals were calculated. The decomposition uses the observed participant-hour frame rather than a site-average grid. The Shapley allocation refits hierarchy-valid nested models and averages both entry orders for site and light source; the interaction enters only after both main effects. Marginal R² was 0.796 for the combined site, light-source, and interaction terms. Conditional R² was 0.876 after adding the participant intercept, a difference of 0.080. The adjusted ICC was 0.394 because it excludes fixed-effect variance from its denominator; the unadjusted ICC was 0.080 on the total model-based variance scale. A one-SD participant intercept was a 2.00-fold conditional expected mean relative to a participant at the model-average intercept while holding site and light source fixed. This is a common participant multiplier across categories, not a participant-specific category response. The variance decomposition is evaluated over observed participant-hours and is not a site-average estimand. Marginal R² has no unique term decomposition. In the hierarchy-respecting Shapley analysis, the study-site component was 0.056 (7.1% of the full marginal R²), the light-source component was 0.710 (89.3%), and the site-by-light-source interaction component was 0.029 (3.7%). The three point allocations sum to the full marginal R². The analysis averages both hierarchy-valid entry orders for site and light source and introduces the interaction only after both main effects. It is consequently invariant to the chosen reference site and light-source category. It remains a descriptive allocation tied to this model-based R² definition and nested-model set, not a unique or causal partition of exposure variance. The fit returned convergence code 0 without warnings, had a positive-definite Hessian, and was not singular. Its lag-one Pearson residual correlation was 0.288, so a participant intercept did not remove all within-participant temporal dependence. Exact zeros comprised 27.8%, compared with 39.8% under the fitted Tweedie distribution. The variance assessment is therefore descriptive, not evidence that the model predicts individual participant-hours well. Its Nakagawa R² values are not numerically interchangeable with the quasi-deviance R² and fixed-effect allocations in the preceding table. All five models used for the Shapley value function likewise converged without warnings, had positive-definite Hessians, and were non-singular. Random-intercept assessment estimates and model diagnostics , together with the hierarchy-respecting Shapley allocation and nested-model checks , provide the complete stored point estimates and checks.

title: H03: Self-reported light source and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Model checks Both population-mean fits converged without warnings, retained full design rank, and had finite positive-definite participant-cluster covariances. Their working distribution nevertheless does not reproduce important features of individual-hour data. Hours close together in time still show similar unexplained deviations: the technical lag-one residual correlations are 0.478 near eye and 0.615 at chest. Participant clustering protects coefficient uncertainty against arbitrary dependence within a participant, but it does not whiten residuals or turn the working Tweedie family into a calibrated probability model. The discrepancy is clearest for zeros. Exact zeros comprise 27.8% of hours, whereas the working Tweedie relationship implies 85.2% near eye and 94.8% at chest. The model is therefore interpreted only as a log-mean model with participant-robust inference, not as an individual-hour prediction model or a model of zero probability. title: H03: Self-reported light source and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Exploratory nonlinear time-of-day context Note Exploratory analysis This nonlinear generalized additive model (GAM) analysis is separate from the preregistered category inference. The association with clock time is allowed to bend across the day rather than follow a straight line. The model uses one global cyclic time-of-day smooth plus sum-to-zero light-source and site deviations, participant curves, participant-day shifts, and a boundary-aware AR(1) correction. Light-source curves are ratios to the global daily smooth, not to indoor electric light, and no curve-wide test is made. The exploratory model uses the untransformed one-hour geometric melEDI outcome with a fixed-power Tweedie mean and log link. This targets the conditional arithmetic mean rather than a back-transformed mean of a log-transformed outcome, which is why its daytime curves are substantially higher than curves for a geometric-scale centre. Site, participant, and participant-day smooths remain in the fitted model but are set to zero in the displayed global and category curves. The temporal model is closer to the primary model’s raw-outcome mean target, but the two displays are not numerically interchangeable. The primary scalar averages over all contributed times and forms a site-average on its fitted log-mean scale. The temporal curves condition on clock time and show only the global and light-source components. Their values therefore need not average to the primary category estimates. Show exploratory nonlinear time-of-day details Figure 5: Exploratory near-eye time-of-day means, ratios to the global smooth, and available participant-hours. Near-eye curve data , ratio data , and clock-time support contain the plotted values and untransformed melEDI. Figure 6: Exploratory chest time-of-day means, ratios to the global smooth, and available participant-hours. Chest curve data , ratio data , and clock-time support contain the plotted values and untransformed melEDI. Global time of day received 60.4% of the near-eye and 58.3% of the chest point allocation. Light-source deviations received 24.2% and 26.4%, site deviations 5.2% and 6.5%, participant curves 7.6% and 5.7%, and participant-day shifts 2.5% and 3.1%. The Shapley allocation averages a component’s contribution across all orders in which components could be added, allocating shared fitted-model information rather than counting it repeatedly. These are point summaries without uncertainty intervals and are not independent or causal percentages of raw melEDI variance. Both final fits converged at full coefficient rank with positive-definite smoothing-parameter Hessians. The chest fit with zero AR correlation, used only to estimate the fixed AR value, did not converge; the final fixed-AR fit did. The global smooths used 9.36 and 9.47 effective degrees of freedom out of ten available, with deterministic k-indices of 0.890 and 0.884. The smooths are therefore close to their basis capacity, and no permutation p -value was computed. The AR adjustment reduces but does not eliminate the tendency for nearby hours to retain similar unexplained deviations: the technical lag-one residual correlations are 0.146 near eye and 0.144 at chest. Residual spread remains fitted-value dependent, and the working zero fractions of 0.465 and 0.508 exceed the observed fractions of 0.278 and 0.277. These limitations confine the temporal analysis to descriptive conditional-mean context. The ribbons are pointwise 95% intervals; they are not simultaneous bands and do not support curve-wide significance claims.

text: Exploratory linear latitude context Latitude cannot be estimated alongside a saturated fixed-site term because each site has only one latitude. A separate exploratory model therefore replaces site with category-specific linear absolute-latitude slopes: geo_medi_1h ~ 0 + light_source + light_source : absolute_latitude_10deg_centered The coefficient for each category is the multiplicative change in expected one-hour melEDI per 10° farther from the equator. Centering at the site-average mean absolute latitude, 39.2° near eye and 38.1° at chest, changes the intercepts but not the slopes. Uncertainty is clustered at site, not participant, because latitude varies only across nine near-eye and eight chest sites. Seven slope p-values receive an FDR adjustment within each placement. FDR adjustment forms one seven-slope family within each placement. The omission columns show how often the slope kept its full-model direction and its point-estimate range. Figure 8: Exploratory factor change in expected melEDI per 10° increase in absolute latitude; points filled in their light-source colour pass the seven-slope within-placement FDR label. Latitude result data , site latitudes , leave-one-site-out fits , and model checks provide the exact exploratory outputs. Near eye showed FDR-labelled positive gradients for indoor electric light (ratio 1.197 per +10°, 95% CI 1.081–1.326), indoor daylight (1.253, 1.131–1.388), outdoor daylight (1.354, 1.105–1.661), and sleep darkness (1.428, 1.076–1.895). Their site-cluster covariance ranks were necessarily limited to eight and seven because only nine and eight independent site clusters were available. Accordingly, the report gives coefficient-wise slope tests and no joint seven-slope Wald test. These are ecological associations across a small number of sites. Absolute latitude may stand in for season, climate, built environment, behaviour, or other site differences; the analysis does not identify a causal latitude effect or show that latitude adequately replaces the supported category-by-site interaction.

title: H03: Self-reported light source and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Interpretation Self-reported primary light source is strongly associated with measured one-hour personal light exposure. Daylight, especially outdoors, corresponds to substantially higher melEDI than indoor electric light, whereas display and sleep-environment categories correspond to lower values. The magnitude of these contrasts varies materially by site. Outdoor electric is especially sparse and site-dependent, so its cross-site descriptive value depends strongly on whether a common category contrast is imposed. The result is observational. It does not show that changing a reported light source causes a particular exposure, predict a health outcome, or establish equivalence between near-eye and chest measurements. Participant-clustered inference, sensitivity analyses, and deletion checks support the overall category conclusion, while residual and zero-mass model checks limit claims about the working Tweedie distribution. The nonlinear time-of-day GAMs add useful descriptive context but remain separate from the preregistered inference. The linear absolute-latitude context identifies several exploratory ecological gradients, but the small number of sites and site-level confounding preclude a causal latitude interpretation.

title: H03: Self-reported light source and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Preregistration deviations Study-site structure ( DEV-013 ). The registered random-effects architecture was not retained because site support did not justify the registered random-slope formulation and the participant-day component collapsed. The accepted analysis uses fixed study-site adjustment for the population-average category association and a separate category-by-site interaction model. Response model ( DEV-014 ). The registered Gaussian response formulation had inadequate distributional diagnostics. The accepted fixed-power quasi-Tweedie log-mean models with participant-clustered covariance accommodate the non-negative, right-skewed response and exact zeros. They are mean models, not calibrated zero-generating distributions. Light-source categories ( DEV-022 ). The analysis retains all seven prespecified categories under one placement-independent support rule and labels unsupported site-category cells rather than silently deleting categories. Primary and site-interaction questions ( DEV-023 ). The additive model supplies the primary six-restriction category omnibus; the separate category-by-site interaction model supplies descriptive means, ratios, and site-specific variation. Multiple-testing adjustment ( DEV-024 ). False-discovery-rate adjustment is applied to each explicitly assembled complete contrast family; category and site-interaction questions remain separate families.

title: H03 analysis preparation and provenance – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: About this analysis record H03 asks whether all seven prespecified self-reported primary-light-source categories are associated with measured one-hour personal light exposure. The primary near-eye sensor position measures light close to the eyes. The complementary chest sensor position measures light at the chest and is not a measure of ocular exposure. The outcome is melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance (melEDI). The central estimand is the site-average geometric expected melEDI for each category and its ratio to indoor electric light. A site-average estimate gives each included site equal weight on the fitted log-mean scale; one back-transformation then returns the estimate to melEDI in lux. This page identifies the data and code that produced the result, explains why each analytical operation was needed, and shows the recorded evidence used to check it. The analysis is observational and does not identify causal effects, health outcomes, or equivalence between measurement placements. The H03 results report presents the scientific findings and its linked registration-record summary . The metric and model-ready input definitions are also documented in Preparation 04 and Preparation 06 . Note Scope of this analysis record This page reads accepted estimates, 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs), omnibus tests, model checks, influence refits, sensitivity results, exploratory smooths, and latitude results from their recorded files. Its bounded display work does not fit or refit a model, calculate predictions, re-estimate residual autocorrelation, rerun a leave-one-site-out analysis, bootstrap, simulate data, or recalculate a variance allocation.

title: H03 analysis preparation and provenance – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
section: Schema, keys, missingness, and category overlap
text: Schema, keys, missingness, and category overlap Outcome and diary records were joined one-to-one by site, participant, local date, and local clock hour. The primary model frames contain only admissible outcome hours with a non-missing primary-light-source category. Each retained record has one analysis category. The normalized diary also retains seven source-indicator flags: 7,109 near-eye hours and 8,012 chest hours had more than one true source flag, but the declared primary category was one of those true flags and remained the single mutually exclusive analysis label. Thus the overlap information was audited without duplicating an hour across categories. Show the R code used for this display integrity_display <- frame_integrity |> transmute ( Placement = .data $ placement, Hours = .data $ observations, ` Duplicate hour keys ` = .data $ duplicate_hour_keys, ` Missing outcomes ` = .data $ missing_outcome, ` Missing categories ` = .data $ missing_category, ` Invalid outcomes ` = .data $ invalid_response, ` Hours below 30 valid minutes ` = .data $ valid_wall_minutes_below_30, ` One source flag ` = .data $ source_flag_one, ` Multiple source flags ` = .data $ source_flag_multiple, ` Category-code conflicts ` = .data $ category_mapping_conflicts ) stopifnot ( all (integrity_display $ ` Duplicate hour keys ` == 0 L), all (integrity_display $ ` Missing outcomes ` == 0 L), all (integrity_display $ ` Missing categories ` == 0 L), all (integrity_display $ ` Invalid outcomes ` == 0 L), all (integrity_display $ ` Hours below 30 valid minutes ` == 0 L), all (integrity_display $ ` Category-code conflicts ` == 0 L) ) integrity_display |> gt :: gt ( rowname_col = "Placement" ) |> gt :: fmt_integer ( columns = where (is.numeric), sep_mark = "," ) |> h03_gt ( 11 ) Table 2: Bounded integrity checks of the accepted primary H03 model frames. text: Primary samples and repeated observations A participant-hour is one accepted participant-by-local-hour record; a participant-day comprises one participant’s accepted hours on one local date. text: 3. Population-mean and category-by-site interaction models

title: H03 analysis preparation and provenance – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Additive population-mean model The prespecified primary question is tested with a population-mean GLM: geo_medi_1h ~ site + light_source geo_medi_1h is the one-hour zero-aware geometric melEDI in lux. The model uses a log link and a quasi-Tweedie variance function Var(Y | X) = phi * mu^1.539919 . Site is a fixed factor with sum contrasts; light source is a fixed seven-level factor with indoor electric light as the treatment reference. The formula contains no random effect. Repeated participant-hours are addressed for inference with participant-clustered HC1 sandwich covariance, finite denominator degrees of freedom equal to the number of participant clusters minus one, and two-sided 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs). This interval calculation accounts for the fact that observations from the same participant may be related. Cluster-robust covariance protects coefficient uncertainty against unspecified within-participant dependence under its large-cluster assumptions; it does not remove serial structure from residuals or change the fitted conditional mean. Participant-day repetition and within-day temporal dependence are therefore also examined directly in model checks and sensitivity analyses. section: Omnibus test, category contrasts, and site-average estimates
text: Omnibus test, category contrasts, and site-average estimates The primary omnibus is a six-restriction Wald F test that all six non-reference light-source coefficients equal zero. The near-eye test is the preregistered primary inference; the chest test is complementary. The six non-reference ratios to indoor electric light form one multiplicity family within placement and receive a false-discovery-rate (FDR) adjustment using the Benjamini–Hochberg method. Category means and ratios are site-average estimates: each site receives equal weight on the fitted log-mean scale before one back-transformation to melEDI in lux. This is a geometric expectation, not the arithmetic mean of response-scale site predictions. title: H03 analysis preparation and provenance – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Category-by-site interaction The association between light-source category and melEDI is allowed to differ by study site in a model examined separately from the additive primary omnibus. The near-eye frame supports the literal interaction: geo_medi_1h ~ site * light_source The chest frame lacks all categories at the near-eye-only Munich (DE) site and is therefore represented by one coefficient for each observed site-category cell: geo_medi_1h ~ 0 + site_source_cell The second expression is an equivalent saturated observed-cell parameterization, not a different scientific estimand. Its restriction matrix tests whether the observed cells can be represented additively by site plus light source. The models use the same log link, quasi-Tweedie variance, participant-clustered HC1 covariance, and geometric site-average estimation as the additive models. text: Descriptive model performance Squared-error and working-deviance summaries were calculated from the full category-by-site interaction models, so the interaction contribution is retained. These quantities describe in-sample fit and are not inferential substitutes for the omnibus tests. The participant-hour version weights every retained hour equally; the participant-balanced version first gives each participant equal total weight. The working-deviance version uses the quasi-Tweedie mean-variance relationship. Because these loss functions differ, their R-squared values are not interchangeable. The Shapley allocation averages a component’s contribution across all orders in which components could be added, allocating shared fitted-model information rather than counting it repeatedly; these are point summaries without uncertainty intervals. text: Exploratory participant random-intercept assessment This separate exploratory model lets each participant have a stable overall exposure level while study site, light source, and their category-by-site interaction remain fixed effects. It was fitted to the accepted near-eye sample of 17,935 participant-hours from 140 participants, 801 participant-days, nine sites, and seven light-source categories. All five hierarchy-valid nested fits converged without warnings, had positive-definite Hessians, and were non-singular. The model contains no random light-source slopes, participant-day effect, or AR(1) term. Residual dependence and the zero process remain imperfectly represented: the lag-one Pearson residual correlation was 0.288, while the observed and Tweedie-implied zero fractions were 0.278 and 0.398. These point summaries are descriptive, model-dependent, non-causal, do not have uncertainty intervals, and are not a unique allocation of exposure variation. The assessment does not replace the accepted population-mean primary model or change its omnibus test or multiplicity families. It is distinct from the separate within-participant and between-participant sensitivity, which is a population-mean quasi-Tweedie augmentation with participant-clustered covariance. That sensitivity is not a mixed model, random-intercept model, random-slope model, or variance-component analysis. The corresponding reader-facing auxiliary result retains the same boundary.

text: Zero mass and residual shape The fixed-power Tweedie working model substantially overpredicted exact zeros: the observed overall fractions were 0.278 near eye and 0.277 at chest, compared with working expectations of 0.852 and 0.948. This is a distributional limitation, not evidence that observed zeros should be removed. The analysis therefore treats the Tweedie family as a working mean-variance model, uses robust covariance, and avoids probability claims about the zero process. text: 5. Predefined sensitivities One sensitivity uses the gap-timing-unaware dataset . It still passes the general requirement of at least 50% valid minutes per hour and at least 80% valid hours per day, but the timing of the remaining missing observations is not used for an additional metric-specific adjustment. At this first explanation only, the primary dataset could be interpreted as a time-sensitive primary metric dataset. Hereafter it is called simply the primary dataset. Other predefined branches use the same participants and participant-hours available at both sensor positions; exclude hours that span diary-state or measurement-context boundaries; exclude site-category cells that fail the predefined support rule; vary the quasi-Tweedie working power to 1.30 and 1.80; and add participant-level category-proportion terms to separate within-participant from between-participant information. The same-participant, same-hour comparison uses separately fitted placement estimates and is not an equivalence test or a direct test of a sensor-position effect. These branches do not replace the primary estimand. title: H03 analysis preparation and provenance – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Nonlinear time-of-day GAM analysis The nonlinear generalized additive model (GAM) analysis is exploratory and separate from the preregistered GLM inference. The association with clock time is allowed to bend across the day rather than follow a straight line. It models the raw one-hour geometric melEDI outcome with a fixed-power Tweedie mean, log link, global cyclic time smooth, sum-to-zero light-source and site deviation smooths, participant-specific smooths, and participant-day random intercepts: geo_medi_1h ~ s (time_hour, bs = "cc" , k = 12 ) + s (time_hour, light_source, bs = "sz" , k = 12 ) + s (time_hour, site, bs = "sz" , k = 12 ) + s (time_hour, participant, bs = "fs" , k = 10 ) + s (participant_day, bs = "re" ) The sum-to-zero smooths add category- and site-specific deviations to the global cyclic time-of-day smooth; indoor electric light is not a smooth reference. bam() used fREML, discrete computation, cyclic knots at 0 and 24 hours, and a second fit with an AR(1) working error parameter estimated from the preliminary standardized residual lag-1 correlation. Participant, participant-day, and site smooths remain in the fitted model but are excluded from the displayed population curves. The stored figure curves form a site-average by giving sites equal weight and then omit unsupported time points from the display. title: H04: Self-reported activity and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: H04: Self-reported activity and measured personal light exposure Associations with one-hour melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance Last modified: August 20, 2026

title: H04: Self-reported activity and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Question The preregistered hypothesis was: H4: Hourly self-reported activity categories predict hourly geometric mean melanopic EDI. This analysis asks whether five interpretable reported activity categories are associated with measured one-hour melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance (melEDI), a melanopsin-weighted measure of illuminance expressed in lux, after accounting for study site. The categories are not mutually exclusive behavioural states: when an hour has several retained labels, its contribution is shared equally among them. Note Answer in brief Reported activity category was associated with near-eye melEDI, F (4, 125) = 83.59, raw p <0.001 . Site-average estimates give each observed study site equal weight on the fitted log-mean scale. The 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) quantify statistical uncertainty while allowing observations from the same participant to be related. Because the activity-by-site interaction, which allows the activity association to differ by study site, was supported, the descriptive means and ratios come from that model. Only the primary five-category omnibus comes from the additive population-mean model. Chest estimates showed the same broad ordering, and all four named-versus-home contrasts retained their direction and classification in every prespecified sensitivity. Other/unspecified activity remains visible as a varied display-only category, not a coherent scientific category, and supports no scientific claim. These are observational associations, not causal effects of changing activity.

title: H04: Self-reported activity and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: What was analysed The near-eye sensor position is primary because it measures light near the eyes, although it is not a retinal measurement. The chest sensor position is complementary and is not a measure of ocular exposure. The positions are fitted separately, and similarity is not interpreted as equivalence. The response is the zero-aware geometric mean melEDI within each hour, including genuine zero values. Before the activity data were reshaped, active travel, outdoor work, and outdoor free time were combined into Outdoors . Duplicate collapsed labels were removed within each participant-hour. If Other was co-selected with a named category, only the named category or categories were retained; Other was kept when it was the sole selection. No diary free text was inspected or recoded. An hour with k retained distinct labels contributes k rows, each with weight 1/k . The total analytical weight of every fitted participant-hour is therefore one. Hours with no retained category are not interpreted as “no activity” and are excluded from the category model. A participant-hour is one original hourly record for one participant. A participant-day groups that participant’s records within one study day.

title: H04: Self-reported activity and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Terms used below Site-average estimate: an average across the observed sites that gives each site equal weight on the fitted log-mean scale. Activity-by-site interaction: a model term that allows the association between activity and melEDI to differ by study site. 95% CI: a confidence interval that summarizes statistical uncertainty around an estimate. FDR: a false-discovery-rate adjustment applied within a declared family of comparisons. Random intercept: a term that lets participants have different overall exposure levels while retaining the fixed activity-by-site structure. Nonlinear GAM analysis: a generalized additive model analysis in which activity- and site-associated patterns may bend across clock time. AR(1): a first-order autoregressive structure that allows adjacent residuals to be more alike than residuals farther apart. Shapley allocation: a descriptive allocation that distributes shared fitted-model information instead of summing overlapping contributions. Common sample: the same participants and participant-hours observed at both sensor positions.

title: H04: Self-reported activity and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Principal activity-category estimates The additive primary model forces every site to share one activity ratio, whereas the activity-by-site interaction model estimates site-specific category means before giving every observed site equal weight on the fitted log-mean scale. The preregistered additive-model omnibus remains the primary inferential test, but the descriptive means, ratios, differences, 95% CIs, and site summaries below use the less restrictive interaction model. Other/unspecified activity is the sole exception: it is excluded from the interaction model and remains visible only as a quiet additive-model display-only estimate. Figure 1: Site-average one-hour melEDI estimates from the activity-by-site interaction model and named-category ratios versus At home; bars are participant-cluster-robust 95% CIs. title: H04: Self-reported activity and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Model and estimand The primary population-mean model estimates the average association between reported activity and melEDI after accounting for site. It uses fixed site and activity terms, a quasi-Tweedie variance function with power 1.539919, a log link, and the exact 1/k prior weights. A separate activity-by-site interaction model allows the association between each of the five interpretable activity categories and melEDI to differ by study site. It is used for descriptive category and site summaries, while the additive model remains the basis for the primary inferential test. Other/unspecified activity remains unrestricted in the additive model and is display-only. Participant-cluster-robust uncertainty allows concurrent category memberships and longitudinal observations from the same participant to be related. The technical implementation uses HC1 covariance and finite-cluster t and F reference distributions, with the number of participant clusters minus one as denominator degrees of freedom. The primary equality test compares Sleeping, At home, vehicle or public-transport travel, indoor or home working, and Outdoors. The fitted Other coefficient remains unrestricted and does not enter that four-row joint restriction. A full six-category omnibus is reported secondarily. Category means are reported as site-average estimates across the sites observed for that sensor position. Every site contributes equally on the fitted log-mean scale. The resulting average is then back-transformed, meaning that it is returned to melEDI in lux. It is therefore the geometric mean of the fitted site-specific means, not an observation-weighted arithmetic mean. At home is the reader-facing comparison reference. The estimand is average melEDI associated with each reported collapsed activity category, with an hour’s contribution shared across concurrently reported categories. It is not a transition effect, an individual-specific effect, or a causal contrast between mutually exclusive behaviours.

title: H04: Self-reported activity and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Exploratory participant random-intercept decomposition The accepted population-mean models use participant-clustered covariance and do not contain random effects. A separate descriptive mixed model was fitted to quantify how much model-based variation is associated with the fixed activity-by-site structure and with participant-level variation. The random intercept lets participants have different overall exposure levels while retaining the fixed activity-by-site structure: geo_medi_1h ~ site * activity_named + ( 1 | participant) The model used a Tweedie distribution with a log link, maximum likelihood, and the same fixed working power of 1.539919. It retained the supported five named categories, so Other-only hours were not included. Every retained participant-hour still contributed exactly one unit through its 1/k membership weights. Five hierarchy-valid models allocated marginal R² to activity, study site, and their interaction. The participant random intercept then supplied the difference between conditional and marginal R². This model has no participant-specific activity slope and no participant-day random effect. It is separate from the population-mean Mundlak-style sensitivity, which adjusts current-category contrasts for each participant’s usual activity composition. Neither assessment changes the primary analysis or its multiplicity families. Table 10: Exploratory fractionally weighted participant random-intercept R² decomposition. Component Quantity Estimate Interpretation Near-eye Model-based R² Marginal R² 0.766 Activity, site, and their interaction Model-based R² Conditional R² 0.858 Fixed effects plus participant intercept Model-based R² Participant-intercept increment 0.092 Conditional minus marginal R² Model-based R² Distribution-specific remainder 0.142 Remainder under the lognormal approximation Participant-level variation Adjusted participant ICC 0.393 Participant share after excluding fixed-effect variance Participant-level variation One-SD participant factor 2.02× Conditional expected-mean factor one participant SD above average Marginal R² allocation Marginal R² allocation 0.618 80.7% of full marginal R² Marginal R² allocation Marginal R² allocation 0.096 12.5% of full marginal R² Marginal R² allocation Marginal R² allocation 0.053 6.9% of full marginal R² Chest Model-based R² Marginal R² 0.768 Activity, site, and their interaction Model-based R² Conditional R² 0.859 Fixed effects plus participant intercept Model-based R² Participant-intercept increment 0.092 Conditional minus marginal R² Model-based R² Distribution-specific remainder 0.141 Remainder under the lognormal approximation Participant-level variation Adjusted participant ICC 0.394 Participant share after excluding fixed-effect variance Participant-level variation One-SD participant factor 2.05× Conditional expected-mean factor one participant SD above average Marginal R² allocation Marginal R² allocation 0.661 86.1% of full marginal R² Marginal R² allocation Marginal R² allocation 0.045 5.9% of full marginal R² Marginal R² allocation Marginal R² allocation 0.061 8.0% of full marginal R² Point estimates use Nakagawa’s lognormal distribution-specific variance convention. The fixed linear predictor uses a fractional-frequency sample variance with exact 1/k weights, so each participant-hour sums to one. No bootstrap intervals were calculated. The allocation averages the two valid entry orders for activity and site, and adds their interaction only after both main effects. Marginal R² was 0.766 near eye and 0.768 at chest. Conditional R² was 0.858 and 0.859, respectively. The participant intercept therefore added about 0.092 at each sensor position. Activity accounted for 80.7% of near-eye and 86.1% of chest marginal R², compared with 12.5% and 5.9% for study site and 6.9% and 8.0% for the interaction. A one-SD participant intercept corresponded to a 2.02-fold near-eye and 2.05-fold chest conditional expected mean while holding activity and site fixed. This common multiplier is not a participant-specific activity slope. All ten nested fits converged without warnings, had positive-definite Hessians, and were non-singular. Aggregated participant-hour Pearson residuals retained lag-one correlations of 0.317 near eye and 0.301 at chest. Observed exact-zero fractions were 0.294 and 0.301, compared with mixed-model Tweedie-implied fractions of 0.410 and 0.429. The decomposition is consequently an exploratory point description, not evidence of calibrated individual-hour prediction or a causal partition. The conventional unweighted expanded-row marginal R² was 0.768 and 0.770, only slightly higher than the required weighted values, but it gives multi-select hours excess influence and is not the reported estimand. These mixed-model R² values are not interchangeable with the quasi-deviance and squared-error summaries above. Random-intercept assessment estimates , model diagnostics , hierarchy-respecting allocation , and nested-model checks provide the complete stored point estimates and checks. Technical mixed-model preparation and variance definitions document the exact weighting and decomposition.

title: H04: Self-reported activity and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Sensitivity analyses The original sensitivity analyses each change a stated part of the accepted analysis: restrict to exactly-one-category hours; retain co-selected Other as a fractionally weighted category; exclude Other-only hours; replace 1/k weights with unit-weight long rows; use gap-timing-unaware data; use the same participants and participant-hours at both sensor positions; change the quasi-Tweedie working power to 1.30 or 1.80; or use the complementary chest sensor position. An additional Mundlak-style sensitivity separates the hourly category contrast from differences in participants’ usual reported activity composition. The gap-timing-unaware dataset still passed the general per-hour and per-day coverage requirements. The term means that the timing of remaining missing observations is not used for an additional metric-specific adjustment; it does not mean that gaps or coverage were ignored. All four named contrasts were stable in every sensitivity at both placements. The deletion audit also removed each site and each of the five highest-score participants in turn; no primary decision changed. These checks support the direction and broad magnitude ordering, but they do not remove the model limitations or upgrade the observational claim. Stable means the direction and prespecified classification were retained. Unit-weight long rows change the estimand by allowing multi-select hours to contribute more than one unit. The within/between participant analysis is an additional exploratory sensitivity. The within-participant category omnibus remained clear near eye, F(4,125)=67.17 , raw p<0.001 , and at chest, F(4,149)=77.86 , raw p<0.001 . Every primary ratio lay inside its Mundlak sensitivity interval. The largest change was the near-eye Outdoors ratio, which decreased by 16.8% from 11.58 to 9.64, with a 95% CI of 6.79 to 13.68. The four named between-participant composition terms were jointly associated with near-eye melEDI, F(4,125)=3.81 , raw p=0.006 , but not clearly with chest melEDI, F(4,149)=2.34 , raw p=0.058 . title: H04: Self-reported activity and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Within- and between-participant activity patterns For this additional sensitivity, each participant’s usual category profile is the fraction of their retained participant-hours assigned to each category after the same 1/k sharing of multi-select hours. The model retains the current reported category and adds the five non-reference participant-level category proportions. The current-category ratios therefore compare reported activity categories after adjustment for participants’ usual activity composition. The between-participant ratios compare a 10 percentage-point higher usual share of the named category with the corresponding lower share of At home, while holding current category, study site, and the other category shares fixed. title: H04: Self-reported activity and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Exploratory time-of-day context Note Exploratory analysis This nonlinear generalized additive model (GAM) analysis is separate from the preregistered category inference. It allows the association with clock time to bend across the day using one cyclic global time-of-day smooth plus thin-plate sum-to-zero activity and site deviations, participant curves, participant-day shifts, and a boundary-aware AR(1) correction that allows adjacent residuals to be more alike than residuals farther apart. Activity curves are also shown as ratios to the global daily smooth, not to At home, and no curve-wide test is made. The exploratory model retains the same activity-long rows and 1/k weights. It contains a cyclic global time smooth, thin-plate sum-to-zero activity and site smooths, participant-specific time smooths, and participant-day random intercepts. Only the global smooth is cyclic. Activity and site deviations may therefore separate at midnight; the open endpoints make this visible and no line wraps from 24:00 to 00:00. Activity-specific autoregressive runs restart at participant-day, activity, repeated-hour, non-consecutive-hour, and gap boundaries. Consequently, concurrent long rows from the same hour never become lag neighbours. The activity smooth improved AIC by 3,215 near eye and 4,984 at chest, while deviance explained increased from 81.8% to 84.8% and from 79.5% to 83.2%. This supports retaining the profiles as descriptive context, not as a second primary activity test. Sleeping had the lowest profiles, whereas Outdoors had the highest daytime profiles. The activity curves use a qualitative palette distinct from the light-source colours used elsewhere in this report series, so colour does not imply a mapping between different category systems. Global time of day received 52.5% of the near-eye and 50.2% of the chest point allocation. Activity deviations received 30.7% and 32.6%, site deviations 5.6% and 6.5%, participant curves 8.4% and 7.1%, and participant-day shifts 2.8% and 3.5%. These are allocations of fitted linear-predictor variation, not independent or causal percentages of raw melEDI variance. Both temporal fits converged at full coefficient rank with positive-definite smoothing-parameter Hessians and no final warnings. Their minimum finite k-indices were 0.872 and 0.863. Residual lag-one correlations remained 0.176 and 0.167, and 41 near-eye plus 40 chest clock/category cells were locally sparse. The non-cyclic deviations can show large endpoint ratios. The working zero fractions of 0.452 and 0.502 exceed the observed fractions of 0.289 and 0.294. The profiles are therefore assessed acceptable with limitation . For each time-by-activity profile, sites are averaged equally on the fitted log-mean scale after participant and participant-day contributions are set to zero. Uncertainty uses the fitted coefficient covariance from stats::vcov(fit, unconditional = TRUE) , with the fitted Vp matrix only as an error fallback, followed by one back-transformation. Ribbons are model-based pointwise 95% CIs: each interval applies to one displayed clock time rather than to the whole curve simultaneously. No time-specific test, significant period, or curve-wide inference is reported. The positive lag-one residual correlations mean that neighbouring hourly residuals remain related despite the working AR(1) correction. No resampling enters the displayed estimates or intervals. title: H04: Self-reported activity and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Interpretation Reported activity is strongly associated with one-hour personal light exposure. Sleeping corresponds to markedly lower melEDI than At home, whereas vehicle or public-transport travel, indoor or home working, and especially Outdoors correspond to higher values. The ordering is similar at chest, and it persists in the exact placement-matched sample and across the predefined sensitivity set. It also persists after adjustment for participants’ usual reported activity composition. Activity-associated means vary materially by site. The result remains observational. Fractional membership is a transparent way to preserve one total contribution per participant-hour; it does not make simultaneously reported labels mutually exclusive or remove ambiguity in self-report timing. Other/unspecified activity is a varied display-only category, not a coherent scientific category, and supports no substantive interpretation. The site-average estimates describe the observed site set and do not automatically generalize to other populations. Participant-clustered inference accommodates within-hour membership and the longitudinal record under the stated mean model, but it does not cure residual serial dependence, fitted-value-dependent spread, sparse site cells, or the model’s limited representation of exact zeros. The time-of-day profiles add descriptive context only, and the separate sensor-position fits do not establish equivalence.

title: H04: Self-reported activity and measured personal light exposure – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Preregistration changes Study-site structure ( DEV-013 ). The accepted population-average category model uses fixed study-site adjustment, while a separate activity-by-site interaction model evaluates variation among sites. The site interaction does not redefine the primary omnibus test. Response model ( DEV-014 ). Fixed-power quasi-Tweedie log-mean models with participant-clustered covariance replace the registered Gaussian mixed model. They describe multiplicative mean comparisons and are not treated as calibrated zero-generating distributions. Multi-label activity representation ( DEV-025 ). The analysis collapses the three outdoor flags before pivoting, removes duplicate labels within an hour, gives each of k concurrent retained categories weight 1/k , and retains Other only when it is the sole selected category for descriptive display. Primary and site-interaction questions ( DEV-026 ). The additive site-plus-activity model supplies the primary activity omnibus; the separate activity-by-site interaction model supplies descriptive category means, ratios, and site-specific variation. Multiple-testing adjustment ( DEV-027 ). False-discovery-rate adjustment is applied to each explicitly assembled complete activity or site-interaction contrast family.

title: H04 analysis preparation and provenance – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: About this analysis record Note About this analysis record This page explains how verified one-hour melEDI records and multi-select self-reported activity reports were turned into the scientific results. The H04 results report presents the findings and its preregistration changes . H04 asks whether hourly self-reported activity categories are associated with hourly geometric mean melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance (melEDI), a melanopsin-weighted measure of illuminance expressed in lux. The primary near-eye sensor position measures light near the eyes but is not a retinal measurement. The complementary chest sensor position is not a measure of ocular exposure. The five interpretable categories are At home, Office/home working, Outdoors, Vehicle/public transport, and Sleeping. Other/unspecified activity remains in the additive population-mean model as a display-only row, is a varied display-only category rather than a coherent scientific category, and supports no substantive claim. Activity categories are not mutually exclusive behavioural states. When an hour contains several retained labels, that hour contributes 1/k to each of its k labels. The central category estimand is therefore average melEDI associated with each reported collapsed activity category, with the hour’s contribution shared across concurrent reports. It is not a causal effect. A participant-hour is one original hourly record for one participant; the concurrent selections share that one hour rather than creating independent duplicates. A participant-day groups that participant’s records within one study day. A site-average estimate is an average across the observed study sites that gives each site equal weight. The activity-by-site interaction model allows the association between activity category and melEDI to differ by study site. This page identifies the data and code that produced the result, explains why each operation was needed, and shows the recorded evidence used to check it. Shared coverage and model-ready dataset definitions are documented in Preparation 02 and Preparation 06 .

text: Activity transformation The diary transformation is outcome-blind. It first combines the three outdoor flags, travel by bicycle/on foot, working outdoors, and free time outdoors, into Outdoors . It then deduplicates collapsed labels within an hour. If Other is selected with a named category, only the named category or categories are retained; Other is retained only when it is the sole selected label. Free text is neither inspected nor recoded. After these operations, the retained distinct labels are pivoted to long format. If hour h contains k_h labels, each long row receives w_{hc}=\frac{1}{k_h}, \qquad \sum_{c=1}^{k_h} w_{hc}=1. Thus an original hour contributes one total unit, whether it supplies one, two, or three activity memberships. Using unweighted long rows would instead estimate a selection-level association in which multi-select hours count more than single-select hours. text: Recorded-frame integrity The recorded primary long frames contain one row for each distinct retained hour/activity membership. A repeated outcome is therefore intentional when an hour has several labels; it is not a repeated independent observation. The integrity checks group those rows back to their original hour and verify the response, participant, participant-day, k , and total weight. text: Population-mean and activity-by-site models

title: H04 analysis preparation and provenance – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Additive population-mean model The primary question is tested with the exact Wilkinson formula: geo_medi_1h ~ site + activity geo_medi_1h is the one-hour zero-aware geometric melEDI in lux. The model uses a log link and the quasi-Tweedie working variance \operatorname{Var}(Y\mid X)=\phi\mu^{1.539919} . Site is a fixed factor with sum contrasts; activity is a fixed six-level factor with At home as the treatment reference. Each long row receives its exact analysis_weight = 1/k . Repeated memberships and longitudinal observations are addressed for inference with participant-clustered HC1 sandwich covariance. Denominator degrees of freedom equal the number of participant clusters minus one, and reported intervals are two-sided 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs). This participant-cluster-robust construction allows observations from the same participant to be related. The formula contains no random effect. Show the R code used for this display tibble :: tribble ( ~ Component, ~ Near_eye, ~ Chest, "Formula" , "geo_medi_1h ~ site + activity" , "geo_medi_1h ~ site + activity" , "Response" , "One-hour zero-aware geometric melEDI (lx)" , "One-hour zero-aware geometric melEDI (lx)" , "Mean and variance" , "Log link; quasi-Tweedie p = 1.539919" , "Log link; quasi-Tweedie p = 1.539919" , "Long-row weight" , "1/k retained labels in the original hour" , "1/k retained labels in the original hour" , "Activity reference" , "At home" , "At home" , "Site" , "Nine-level fixed factor; sum contrasts" , "Eight-level fixed factor; sum contrasts" , "Uncertainty" , "Participant-clustered HC1; df = 125" , "Participant-clustered HC1; df = 149" , "Reported named-category mean" , "Site-average estimate from the supported interaction model" , "Site-average estimate from the supported interaction model" , "Role" , "Primary inference" , "Complementary evidence" ) |> gt :: gt () |> gt :: cols_label ( Near_eye = "Near eye" , Chest = "Chest" ) |> gt :: cols_width ( Component ~ gt :: pct ( 21 ), Near_eye ~ gt :: pct ( 39.5 ), Chest ~ gt :: pct ( 39.5 ) ) |> h04_gt ( 11 ) Table 10: Primary and complementary population-mean model settings. Component Near eye Chest Formula geo_medi_1h ~ site + activity geo_medi_1h ~ site + activity Response One-hour zero-aware geometric melEDI (lx) One-hour zero-aware geometric melEDI (lx) Mean and variance Log link; quasi-Tweedie p = 1.539919 Log link; quasi-Tweedie p = 1.539919 Long-row weight 1/k retained labels in the original hour 1/k retained labels in the original hour Activity reference At home At home Site Nine-level fixed factor; sum contrasts Eight-level fixed factor; sum contrasts Uncertainty Participant-clustered HC1; df = 125 Participant-clustered HC1; df = 149 Reported named-category mean Site-average estimate from the supported interaction model Site-average estimate from the supported interaction model Role Primary inference Complementary evidence Cluster-robust covariance protects coefficient uncertainty against unspecified within-participant dependence under its large-cluster assumptions. It does not remove serial structure from residuals or make the working Tweedie distribution a calibrated model of the exact-zero process.

Sites contribute equal weight, the design rows are averaged, and one exponential back-transformation is applied, returning the site-average estimate to melEDI in lux. text: Activity-by-site interaction The activity-by-site interaction is examined separately from the additive primary omnibus with the five interpretable categories. title: H04 analysis preparation and provenance – Nature Health analysis and manuscript
text: Exploratory participant random-intercept decomposition The population-mean quasi-Tweedie GLM and participant-clustered covariance remain the inferential analysis. A separate mixed model describes participant-level variation in the support-qualified five-category activity-by-site frame. The random intercept lets participants have different overall exposure levels while retaining the fixed activity-by-site structure: geo_medi_1h ~ site * activity_named + ( 1 | participant) The generalized linear mixed model was fitted in R with glmmTMB , using a Tweedie distribution with a log link, maximum likelihood, and the fixed working power 1.539919. The exact analysis_weight = 1/k enters every fit. Other-only hours are absent because this branch inherits the supported five-named-category interaction frame. The near-eye fit therefore uses 16,875 long rows representing 16,135 participant-hours from 126 participants. The chest fit uses 20,440 long rows representing 19,497 participant-hours from 150 participants. This descriptive mixed-model decomposition is distinct from the population-mean Mundlak-style sensitivity, which adjusts current-category contrasts for participants’ usual activity composition. Neither assessment changes the primary analysis or its multiplicity families. The standard Nakagawa implementation calculates the fixed-predictor variance with an unweighted variance across fitted rows. That convention would give a multi-select hour more influence because it has more rows. The H04 calculation instead uses the fractional-frequency sample variance \sigma_f^2 = \frac{\sum_i w_i(\eta_i-\bar\eta_w)^2}{\sum_i w_i-1}, \qquad \bar\eta_w = \frac{\sum_i w_i\eta_i}{\sum_i w_i}, where w_i=1/k and \eta_i is the fixed-effects linear predictor. This reduces exactly to the H03 convention when every hour has one row. The participant-intercept variance \sigma_u^2 and the lognormal distribution-specific variance \sigma_e^2 follow the same insight::get_variance() convention. The reported values are R_m^2 = \frac{\sigma_f^2}{\sigma_f^2+\sigma_u^2+\sigma_e^2}, \qquad R_c^2 = \frac{\sigma_f^2+\sigma_u^2} {\sigma_f^2+\sigma_u^2+\sigma_e^2}. All quantities are point estimates without bootstrap intervals." ) |> h04_gt ( 9.2 ) Table 16: Stored fractionally weighted mixed-model R² and participant-intercept summaries. All quantities are point estimates without bootstrap intervals. The marginal fixed-effect R² has no unique term decomposition. A hierarchy-respecting Shapley value function refits these five weighted models: geo_medi_1h ~ 1 + ( 1 | participant) geo_medi_1h ~ site + ( 1 | participant) geo_medi_1h ~ activity_named + ( 1 | participant) geo_medi_1h ~ site + activity_named + ( 1 | participant) geo_medi_1h ~ site * activity_named + ( 1 | participant) Site and activity are averaged over both admissible entry orders. It has no random activity slopes, participant-day intercept, residual correlation structure, or uncertainty intervals, and it does not replace the accepted population-mean inference. section: Convergence, rank, covariance, and residual structure
text: Convergence, rank, covariance, and residual structure Weighted long-row residual contributions are combined back to one value per original hour before the residual-shape, calibration, zero-mass, and serial dependence summaries are formed. Concurrent memberships are therefore not treated as separate model-check observations. Show the R code used for this display main_diagnostics <- model_diagnostics |> filter (.data $ scenario_id == "primary_dataset" ) |> mutate ( placement = factor ( .data $ placement, levels = c ( "Near-eye" , "Chest" ) ) ) |> arrange (.data $ placement) overall_assessment <- diagnostic_assessments |> filter (.data $ diagnostic == "Overall primary mean-model assessment" ) |> select ( "placement" , "assessment" ) main_diagnostics |> left_join (overall_assessment, by = "placement" , relationship = "one-to-one" ) |> transmute ( Placement = as.character (.data $ placement), Converged = if_else (.data $ converged, "Yes" , "No" ), ` Design rank ` = paste0 (.data $ design_rank, "/" , .data $ design_columns), ` Robust covariance positive definite ` = if_else ( .data $ covariance_positive_definite, "Yes" , "No" ), Dispersion = .data $ dispersion, ` Hour residual SD ` = .data $ hour_pearson_sd, ` Residual lag 1 ` = .data $ hour_residual_lag1_correlation, ` Maximum cluster score share ` = .data $ maximum_cluster_score_share, ` Maximum cluster leverage share ` = .data $ maximum_cluster_leverage_share, Assessment = tolower (.data $ assessment) ) |> gt :: gt ( rowname_col = "Placement" ) |> gt :: fmt_number ( columns = c (Dispersion, ` Hour residual SD ` ), decimals = 1 ) |> gt :: fmt_number ( columns = c ( ` Residual lag 1 ` , ` Maximum cluster score share ` , ` Maximum cluster leverage share ` ), decimals = 3 ) |> h04_gt ( 9.8 ) Table 20: Recorded model checks for the additive primary and complementary GLMs. Converged Design rank Robust covariance positive definite Dispersion Hour residual SD Residual lag 1 Maximum cluster score share Maximum cluster leverage share Assessment Near-eye Yes 14/14 Yes 174.2 13.3 0.445 0.398 0.016 acceptable with limitation Chest Yes 13/13 Yes 279.0 16.8 0.498 0.243 0.013 acceptable with limitation Both additive models converged without warnings, were full rank, and retained finite positive-definite participant-clustered covariance. text: Deterministic influence checks Every site was removed once within each placement. The five participants with the largest cluster-score contribution were also removed once within each placement. The model family, formula, weight definition, contrast direction, and site-average estimation rule were preserved.
